title: Rejected temporary-Datalog proposals paused for user confirmation instead of feeding back to the model for retry
description: Follow-up to 3cq, live repro 2026-07-08 session pid-0e8dc2f0: BYOK model omitted '.output answer'; validation rejected the proposal but the turn still paused with a confirmation card for a program that could never execute; approving replayed the rejection ('Temporary Datalog must output exactly answer(x:symbol).'). Fix: _propose_temporary_datalog returns status=rejected (code tool.proposal_rejected) with diagnostics + the authoring contract in the message; the harness's normal tool loop feeds it back so the model revises and re-proposes within the same turn (bounded by max_rounds=20). Only safe_to_confirm proposals pause for the user.
close_reason: Rejected proposals now bounce back to the model with diagnostics + authoring contract for same-turn retry; only executable proposals reach the confirmation card. Committed.

title: PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineers need a trustworthy way to ask questions about a DEXPI 1.3 source file without receiving non-deterministic or hallucinated answers from graph RAG or free-form LLM QA.

The current repository can extract a pyDEXPI full graph, persist a canonical base fact layer, derive an initial generic graph utility layer, and run a narrow pump discharge-path verifier. What it does not yet prove is whether Souffle can serve as the deterministic QA and verification engine over those generated facts.

The user wants to preserve the key product principle: LLMs may help classify, route, and explain questions later, but compliance answers must come from deterministic query outputs. Before adding any LLM integration, the backend must demonstrate that generated Datalog facts can answer useful P&ID topology questions, expose missing facts and predicates clearly, and preserve query results as auditable artifacts.

## Solution

Build the first deterministic P&ID QA query layer around generated derived graph semantics.

The solution should enrich the derived Datalog fact surface with enough base object facts to make query output interpretable, starting with node and node_label facts. It should add a small query corpus that records supported, unsupported, and future candidate P&ID QA questions in an engine-portable way. It should add a CLI query harness that runs a supported known-object topology query against an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file using Souffle, prints readable terminal output, persists the combined Souffle program, persists a JSON result artifact, and keeps raw Souffle output files in an internal output directory.

The first supported query should compare reachable targets and downstream_reference targets for a known source object ID. The first near-term unsupported query should be a pump discharge path classification question. A harder manual-valve-before-check-valve question should be recorded as a future candidate so the system does not overfit only easy queries.

The query corpus should explicitly encode determinism requirements and LLM role constraints. LLM integration is out of scope for this PRD, but the corpus should make future LLM routing safe by documenting that LLMs may classify questions, route to deterministic queries, and explain deterministic results, but may not produce compliance answers without deterministic query output.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want to ask deterministic questions about a DEXPI 1.3 source file, so that I can trust the answer is repeatable and auditable.
2. As a process engineer, I want QA answers to come from deterministic query execution rather than free-form LLM generation, so that compliance answers do not vary between runs.
3. As a process engineer, I want to provide a known object ID and see what objects are reachable from it, so that I can inspect the topology around a specific P&ID object.
4. As a process engineer, I want to compare reachable targets with downstream_reference targets, so that I can understand whether the generic graph utility layer is too broad or too narrow.
5. As a process engineer, I want query output to show full object IDs and object labels, so that results are exact and still readable.
6. As a process engineer, I want empty query results to be treated as successful answers, so that no-result cases can teach us about isolated objects or missing semantics.
7. As a process engineer, I want a warning when the provided source ID is absent from node facts, so that I can distinguish an empty answer from a likely wrong ID.
8. As a process engineer, I want the system to clearly say when a question is unsupported, so that I do not receive a misleading answer.
9. As a process engineer, I want unsupported questions to explain whether facts or predicates are missing, so that I know what capability must be built next.
10. As a process engineer, I want future thermodynamic or hydraulic questions to be identified as requiring external calculation when appropriate, so that Datalog is not overclaimed as a physics engine.
11. As a process engineer, I want the near-term north-star query to trace and classify a centrifugal pump discharge path, so that the QA layer grows toward realistic P&ID review tasks.
12. As a process engineer, I want harder valve-ordering questions to remain visible as future candidates, so that the roadmap reflects realistic engineering concerns.
13. As a maintainer, I want graph_facts.json to remain the canonical base fact layer, so that extraction output stays stable and auditable.
14. As a maintainer, I want Souffle to be evaluated as the deterministic QA and verification engine, so that rule answers can be fast and repeatable.
15. As a maintainer, I want Python to orchestrate extraction, Datalog generation, Souffle execution, and artifact persistence, so that Python is not the source of truth for compliance answers.
16. As a maintainer, I want derived_graph_semantics.dl to include node and node_label facts, so that Datalog queries can produce readable P&ID information without falling back to graph_facts.json for every label.
17. As a maintainer, I want the query harness to operate on an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file first, so that the first slice directly tests the artifact users want to query.
18. As a maintainer, I want the long-term design to allow querying from graph_facts.json directly, so that later workflows can generate and query Datalog in one command.
19. As a maintainer, I want missing Souffle installation to produce a clear diagnostic, so that setup problems are not confused with query failures.
20. As a maintainer, I want Souffle syntax or runtime failures to be treated as failed query execution, so that invalid query programs are surfaced clearly.
21. As a maintainer, I want unsupported corpus entries to return structured unsupported diagnostics, so that unsupported questions are first-class product outputs rather than errors.
22. As a maintainer, I want the query corpus to be separate from compliance rule YAML, so that QA questions do not get confused with promoted validation rules.
23. As a maintainer, I want one YAML file per query corpus entry, so that each query can have its own lifecycle, documentation, and promotion status.
24. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include determinism metadata, so that the engine and source-of-truth assumptions are explicit.
25. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include allowed and disallowed LLM roles, so that future LLM integration does not bypass deterministic execution.
26. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include engine candidates such as Souffle and ErgoAI, so that the query library stays portable across deterministic engines.
27. As a maintainer, I want ErgoAI to remain a future engine candidate rather than an immediate dependency, so that the first slice tests the fact model before changing reasoning engines.
28. As a maintainer, I want the first query harness to read the query corpus entry minimally, so that the corpus becomes load-bearing without requiring a generic query interpreter too early.
29. As a maintainer, I want the first supported query implementation to be explicit and narrow, so that the team learns from real query output before inventing a broad abstraction.
30. As a maintainer, I want the combined Souffle program that actually ran to be persisted, so that users can inspect and rerun the exact query.
31. As a maintainer, I want the generated temporary query Datalog text included in the JSON result artifact, so that query behavior remains explainable.
32. As a maintainer, I want raw Souffle output files kept in an internal subdirectory, so that advanced users can inspect them while the top-level output remains readable.
33. As a maintainer, I want query output files to be overwritten during early experimentation, so that the learning loop stays low-friction.
34. As a maintainer, I want persisted JSON query artifacts, so that query behavior can become regression-tested and compared across fixtures.
35. As a maintainer, I want terminal output for the first query, so that hands-on learning stays tangible.
36. As a future LLM integrator, I want a query corpus with supported and unsupported entries, so that an LLM can later classify and route questions safely.
37. As a future LLM integrator, I want deterministic query outputs to be the only source of compliance answers, so that natural-language explanations remain grounded.
38. As a future rule author, I want the query corpus to reveal missing predicates, so that the P&ID query library grows from real questions instead of imagined ontology.
39. As a future rule author, I want the CodeQL-style library idea to grow from supported queries, so that raw graph facts become stable engineering predicates, reusable path predicates, and validation templates only when needed.
40. As a reviewer, I want the first query corpus to include a future candidate that is too hard today, so that the project does not optimize only for easy topology questions.
41. As a reviewer, I want the query corpus to classify unsupported questions by reason, so that missing data, missing predicates, external calculations, and ambiguity are not conflated.
42. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between unsupported_missing_facts and unsupported_missing_predicates, so that the roadmap can separate extraction work from query-library work.
43. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between unsupported_external_calculation and deterministic graph QA, so that thermodynamics and hydraulics are not accidentally oversold.
44. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between needs_human_clarification and deterministic query execution, so that ambiguous engineering questions are handled honestly.
45. As a reviewer, I want the first deterministic QA seam to be tested through the CLI and persisted artifacts, so that behavior is verified at the same level users experience it.

## Implementation Decisions

- The canonical base fact layer remains graph_facts.json.
- Souffle is the current deterministic engine for the first QA viability slice.
- Python remains the orchestration Adapter for generation, execution, diagnostics, terminal rendering, and artifact persistence.
- LLM integration is explicitly deferred until deterministic tools and query corpus semantics are established.
- The derived graph semantics output should be enriched with node and node_label facts.
- The first query harness operates on an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file.
- The first supported query compares reachable and downstream_reference results for a known source object ID.
- The command should accept a query ID and load the corresponding query corpus entry.
- The command should support the first query ID with explicit implementation rather than a generic YAML-driven query interpreter.
- Unsupported query corpus entries should produce structured unsupported artifacts, not unknown-query errors.
- Missing Souffle should produce a clear diagnostic and failed status.
- Empty result sets should produce successful query artifacts.
- Source ID absence should produce a warning when node facts make validation possible, not a failed status.
- Terminal output should include full target IDs and labels.
- JSON output should include status, diagnostics, query metadata, source ID, generated query Datalog, combined program path, raw output directory, and result sets.
- The combined Souffle program should be persisted as a first-class artifact.
- Raw Souffle output files should be placed under an internal output subdirectory.
- Query output files may be overwritten during the viability phase.
- Query corpus entries should live under queries/corpus as separate YAML files.
- The first corpus entry should be compare_known_object_reachability with supported_deterministic status.
- The near-term target corpus entry should be classify_pump_discharge_path with unsupported_missing_predicates status.
- The advanced future candidate should be manual_valve_before_check_valve_with_exceptions with future_candidate status.
- Query corpus entries should include determinism metadata, current engine, future engine candidates, and LLM role constraints.
- ErgoAI should be documented as a future engine candidate for richer explanations, exceptions, and semantic-rule authoring, not adopted in the first slice.
- The long-term concept is a P&ID query library inspired by CodeQL: raw graph facts to stable engineering predicates to reusable path predicates to validation templates.
- The corpus should be engine-portable and should not make Souffle the only possible long-term reasoning engine.
- The near-term north-star query is pump discharge path classification rather than the more advanced manual-valve-before-check-valve query.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests should verify behavior through public interfaces and persisted artifacts, not private helper structure.
- The highest test seam for the first slice is the CLI query command over a generated derived graph semantics file.
- Tests should run the query command against a representative fixture and assert terminal-visible behavior plus persisted JSON artifact shape.
- Tests should verify that derive-graph-semantics emits node and node_label facts as part of the generated Datalog artifact.
- Tests should verify that the first supported query returns successful output even when one or both result sets are empty.
- Tests should verify that absent source IDs produce warning diagnostics rather than failed execution.
- Tests should verify missing Souffle handling if feasible without depending on the developer machine PATH; if not feasible, isolate that behavior behind the command seam with controlled PATH configuration.
- Tests should verify unsupported corpus entries return structured unsupported diagnostics.
- Tests should verify the combined Souffle program is persisted and includes the generated query Datalog.
- Tests should verify raw Souffle output files are placed under an internal subdirectory.
- Tests should verify the checked-in query corpus entries include determinism and LLM-role metadata.
- Existing prior art includes CLI-style tests for export-facts, derive-graph-semantics, verify-suite, verify-raw-fixture, and compile-rule.
- Existing prior art also includes persisted artifact assertions for graph facts, derived graph semantics, verifier results, and behavioral harness summaries.
- The tests should extend those existing black-box seams rather than introducing internal mocks.
- The first implementation should use red-green vertical slices: one behavior test, minimal implementation, repeat.

## Out of Scope

- LLM integration.
- Natural-language question classification.
- RAG or MCP routing.
- OmniTQA implementation.
- ErgoAI integration.
- A generic query language interpreter over YAML corpus files.
- Full support for arbitrary user-generated P&ID questions.
- Full compliance rule authoring.
- Thermodynamic, hydraulic, sizing, or simulation calculations.
- DEXPI 2.0 ingestion.
- Replacing graph_facts.json as the canonical base fact layer.
- Making Python the source of truth for compliance answers.
- Immutable production run directories for query artifacts.
- A polished process engineer UI.
- Full path provenance or ordered path reconstruction beyond what the first query needs.
- Supporting the advanced manual-valve-before-check-valve query in the first slice.
- Promoting unsupported corpus entries to trusted validation rules.

## Further Notes

The key product principle is: the LLM can help ask, route, and explain the question, but deterministic tools must answer compliance questions.

The first implementation should be treated as a Souffle QA viability slice. It should be allowed to reveal that current predicates are too broad, too narrow, or missing. That learning is valuable and should drive the next predicates in the P&ID query library.

The strongest external architecture analogues are CodeQL for layered query libraries and query metadata, OPA for deterministic policy decisions and diagnostics, osquery for exposing messy domain state through stable queryable relations, and Semgrep or dbt-style registries for curated query/rule corpora with examples and tests.

The most important immediate learning is whether generated Datalog artifacts can support useful known-object topology QA before the project invests in YAML-to-rule compilation, LLM routing, or a larger semantic-rule engine.

title: Verify email addresses at sign-up
description:
Sign-up issues a session for any address, verified or not: the API returns emailVerified false alongside a valid token. Better Auth implements verification completely -- token, expiry, the verify route, resend on sign-in, and auto sign-in afterwards. It was never configured, for the same reason password reset was not: there was no way to send the message. Bead 2qdw added one.

Reading the sign-in path shows why the two settings cannot be separated. When requireEmailVerification is true and sendVerificationEmail is absent, sign-in throws EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED with no route to a token, so every account is locked out permanently. Verification therefore follows the same configured-or-absent rule as the reset link: SMTP present means addresses are verified and enforced; SMTP absent leaves sign-up exactly as it is today rather than bricking the instance.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] With SMTP configured, sign-up sends a verification link
- [ ] An unverified user cannot sign in, and is told why
- [ ] A blocked sign-in resends the link rather than dead-ending
- [ ] Following the link verifies the address and signs the user in
- [ ] With no SMTP, sign-up and sign-in behave exactly as before
- [ ] The link expires and cannot verify a different address
- [ ] Proven against a real SMTP server, not a mock
close_reason: Email verification is enforced whenever SMTP is configured, proven against a real mail server. Sign-up now issues no session; sign-in before confirming returns 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED and resends the link; following the link verifies the address, sets a session, and a subsequent sign-in returns emailVerified true. Replaying the link grants no session, and the token carries one email claim expiring in a day. With no SMTP, sign-up and sign-in are byte-for-byte as before -- confirmed by running that path separately -- because Better Auth's sign-in code throws EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED with no route to a token when enforcement is on and no sender exists, which would lock every account out permanently. That is why requireEmailVerification and sendVerificationEmail are set in the same branch and can never diverge. 136 frontend tests, typecheck, ruff and oxlint clean. README, SECURITY and CHANGELOG no longer claim addresses are unverified.

title: Delete legacy query corpus, rule compiler, and XML-normalization paths
description:
## Problem

After reorganizing the package by pipeline seams, several compatibility paths still keep old architecture alive:

- queries/corpus/ YAML query entries and the query-derived-graph corpus loader.
- rules/ YAML inputs and compiled rule artifacts used by compile-rule tests.
- pydexpi_datalog/_legacy/ XML-direct normalization and cache paths used by dry-run/review-only compatibility behavior.
- Legacy JSON rule evaluation and patch proposal paths that depend on XML-direct normalized objects rather than graph-mirrored facts or LLM-native logic requests.

These paths assume humans hand-author structured YAML/query/rule files. In the LLM-native architecture, the user-facing authoring seam is a logic request: the LLM drafts Datalog plus an English restatement as an in-memory or persisted logic-request artifact, while deterministic execution remains the answer source.

## What to build

Delete the legacy query corpus, rule compiler artifacts, and XML-direct normalization paths. Keep or replace only the behavior that still belongs in the current architecture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Delete queries/corpus/ and remove code/tests/docs that require YAML query-corpus entries.
- [ ] Delete rules/ and remove the compile-rule command, compiler tests, and compiled-rule fixture expectations unless a current non-legacy workflow still needs them.
- [ ] Delete pydexpi_datalog/_legacy/ and tests/_legacy/.
- [ ] Remove dry-run and review-only dependencies on legacy XML normalization/cache artifacts, or replace them with graph-facts/derived-semantics based behavior.
- [ ] Remove or rewrite legacy JSON rule evaluation and patch proposal tests that assume XML-direct normalized objects.
- [ ] Update README and docs so they describe the LLM-native logic-request path and no longer present YAML query/rule authoring as a supported workflow.
- [ ] Public CLI help no longer advertises removed commands.
- [ ] Full test suite passes after obsolete tests are removed or replaced.

## Notes

This is intentionally behavior-breaking cleanup. Do not treat it as a compatibility-preserving refactor. If a command or test only exists to preserve the old hand-authored YAML/query/rule workflow, remove it rather than moving it.

Keep the stable deterministic substrate:

- DEXPI source file to pyDEXPI full graph.
- graph_facts.json base fact artifact.
- graph_facts.dl and derived_graph_semantics.dl.
- BYOK logic requests that can draft Datalog and restatements against the approved predicate contract.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.8

title: Google and Apple sign-in, configured or absent
description:
The hosted profile offers email and password only. Better Auth 1.6.25 ships apple and google as built-in social providers, so this is configuration rather than a new dependency -- which is what lib/auth.ts already claims in a comment.

The design constraint is that a provider must appear in the UI only when it is actually configured. A Google button that 500s because nobody set the credentials is worse than no button, and it is the same silent-failure shape ADR 0016 rejects elsewhere: build_key_store returns None locally and the endpoints answer 404 rather than pretending to have a store.

Half-configuration must be loud. An operator who sets GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and forgets the secret has clearly asked for Google and would otherwise get silence. Refuse to boot and name the missing variable, the way authSecret() and hosted_auth.py already do.

One pure function decides which providers are on, from env alone. auth.ts uses it to build socialProviders; the sign-in page uses it to decide which buttons to render, so the two cannot disagree.

Out of scope, tracked separately: phone number and magic link. Neither is configuration -- both are plugins needing an external sender (SMS, email), which is a real new external boundary and a product decision.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] A pure function maps env to configured providers and is unit tested
- [ ] Google appears only when both its variables are set
- [ ] Apple appears only when both its variables are set
- [ ] Setting one variable of a pair fails at boot naming the missing one
- [ ] The sign-in page renders a button per configured provider and none otherwise
- [ ] Email and password keeps working with no providers configured
- [ ] The local profile still constructs no auth at all
- [ ] Client-visible data carries provider ids, never secrets
- [ ] README documents the variables and Apple's HTTPS and secret-rotation constraints
close_reason: Google and Apple are configured through one pure function that both auth.ts and the sign-in page read, so a button cannot exist for a provider this deployment did not configure. Verified against the running hosted app: with nothing set the page renders email and password alone and zero social buttons; with Google set the button appears, POST /api/auth/sign-in/social returns a real Google authorize URL with PKCE, and unconfigured Apple is refused with PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND. Neither the client id nor the secret appears in the served HTML. Half a credential pair fails the page with a message naming the missing variable, confirmed at runtime after I caught my own first attempt passing spuriously on a leaked shell variable. 9 new unit tests, 123 frontend tests green, typecheck and oxlint clean. Phone number and passwordless email are filed separately as lruc and 1iep: both need an external sender, so neither is configuration.

title: PRD: Hybrid rule packs — advisory guidance, explicit promote, generic Souffle runner
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineers want MikeOSS-like rule packs—markdown skills for HAZOP, EPA,
and similar review frameworks—but also need a neuro-symbolic engine that can
honestly execute some checks against a prepared P&ID. Today those needs are
collapsed or over-promised: the demo process-safety pack runs real Souffle for
two curated rules, yet still through per-rule Python adapters; user markdown
upload (bead 311) was specified as async deontic compile-on-upload before
attach; and raw regulation/HAZOP highlights cannot safely become trusted
executable logic in bulk. Engineers therefore cannot tell advisory guidance
from engine-backed verdicts, and the product cannot prove that a user-promoted
clause runs the same way bundled demo rules do.

## Solution

Ship hybrid rule packs with a hard trust split. Markdown may include advisory
pack guidance (including pasted policy excerpts) and zero or more rules.
Attach injects advisory guidance as attached pack skill context. Rule-pack run
applies what the pack can do: evaluate promoted rules deterministically when
any exist; if advisory-only, run an agentic walkthrough without emitting rule
evaluation outcomes. Compilation never runs on ingest. An explicit per-clause
promote creates a draft rule (engineer-readable rule restatement + candidate
Datalog) only inside the expressible predicate island; outside it, abstain and
keep the clause advisory. All executable rules—bundled and authored—run
through one generic runner under a fixed rule outcome convention (displayed
fence == executed program). Completion bar is one hybrid pack vertical slice:
ingest → attach → promote → run → in-thread evidence for at least one
user-promoted rule.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want to upload a markdown rule pack immediately, so that I am not blocked waiting for bulk compilation.
2. As a process engineer, I want pasted HAZOP or EPA highlights to land as advisory pack guidance by default, so that regulation text is not silently treated as trusted executable logic.
3. As a process engineer, I want advisory pack guidance and rules visually distinguished in browse and detail views, so that I never confuse a checklist with an engine verdict.
4. As a process engineer, I want to attach a hybrid pack to a chat and have its advisory guidance become attached pack skill context, so that the agent can follow the pack’s review style without inventing compliance findings.
5. As a process engineer, I want attach to load skill context without running checks, so that loading a pack is reversible and non-destructive.
6. As a process engineer, I want rule-pack run on an advisory-only pack to walk the checklist in-thread without emitting satisfied/violated outcomes, so that MikeOSS-like workflows still work before any clause is promoted.
7. As a process engineer, I want rule-pack run on a pack with promoted rules to evaluate those rules deterministically and show in-thread rule results with evidence, so that engine-backed checks are explicit and inspectable.
8. As a process engineer, I want rule-pack run on a mixed pack to evaluate rules and optionally use advisory guidance in the same apply action, so that one pack can guide review and execute the crisp subset.
9. As a process engineer, I want to explicitly promote one advisory clause into a draft rule, so that compilation is intentional rather than automatic on upload.
10. As a process engineer, I want promotion to produce an engineer-readable rule restatement and candidate Datalog only when the clause fits the expressible predicate island, so that topology/attribute checks can become real rules.
11. As a process engineer, I want promotion to abstain clearly when a clause needs external formulas, adequacy judgment, or open-ended exceptions, so that the clause stays advisory instead of becoming fake logic.
12. As a process engineer, I want to review and promote a draft rule into an authored rule pack under author-confirmed rule trust, so that later runs of that exact version do not re-prompt confirmation.
13. As a process engineer, I want any edit to promoted logic to create a new version requiring fresh promotion, so that trust never silently carries across changed fences.
14. As a process engineer, I want authored packs never elevated to bundled rule-pack trust, so that maintainer-reviewed demos stay distinct from personal packs.
15. As a process engineer, I want every executable rule—bundled or authored—to emit the same outcome vocabulary (satisfied, violated, indeterminate) and scoped evidence, so that the UI and tests share one contract.
16. As a process engineer, I want missing source numerics or incomplete boundaries to surface as indeterminate / source_data_unavailable rather than invented values, so that honesty beats forced yes/no.
17. As a process engineer, I want the Datalog shown for a rule to be exactly what Souffle executes, so that displayed equals executed.
18. As a process engineer, I want a newly promoted rule to run through the generic runner without a new hand-written Python adapter, so that authoring does not require a code change per clause.
19. As a process engineer, I want the two demo process-safety rules migrated onto that same generic runner, so that curated and authored paths do not diverge.
20. As a process engineer, I want recurring abstentions for clause shapes groundable in DEXPI facts to drive grow-on-demand predicate or export extensions, so that the expressible predicate island can expand without becoming an unbounded regulation compiler.
21. As a process engineer, I want OSS v1 to stay on stratified Souffle/Datalog without ASP, so that defeasible EPA/HAZOP prose does not block shipping hybrid packs.
22. As a process engineer, I want future session exception facts (scoped waivers) to be able to make some “unless” cases crisp in Datalog later, so that exceptions are engineer-entered data rather than model-inferred suppression.
23. As a process engineer, I want pre-made packs that claim trusted executable rules on upload without promotion to be rejected, so that silent trusted import cannot bypass review.
24. As a process engineer, I want a single end-to-end hybrid pack vertical slice to prove the bet, so that “Souffle is real” means user-promoted logic—not only two curated demos.
25. As a developer, I want existing bundled-rule outcome/evidence tests to keep passing against the generic runner, so that migration has a built-in regression net.
26. As a developer, I want markdown parse tests to accept hybrid documents with advisory sections and zero or more fenced rules, so that packaging stays canonical.
27. As a developer, I want review-session HTTP tests to cover ingest, load/attach, promote, and run wiring, so that the product boundary matches the engine contract.
28. As a developer, I want bead 311’s compile-on-upload contract superseded by this PRD, so that agents do not implement the rejected bulk deontic compiler.
29. As a maintainer, I want advisory-only agent notes never labeled as rule evaluation outcomes, so that soft checklist commentary cannot be mistaken for findings.
30. As a maintainer, I want orchestration/order-of-rule-execution machinery out of this slice, so that declarative checks plus optional skill guidance remain the model.

## Implementation Decisions

- Treat a rule pack as a hybrid document: advisory pack guidance plus zero or more rules; only rules produce rule evaluation outcomes (ADR 0013).
- Markdown pack ingest accepts user markdown immediately; default content is advisory; no async compile-on-upload gate; packs are attachable while advisory-only.
- Rewrite/supersede bead 311’s “deontic compilation before attach” contract; keep the MikeOSS-inspired create/upload UX intent without bulk compilation.
- Extend markdown parsing so hybrid packs can carry advisory sections without requiring a fence per section; executable rules still require restatement + fenced souffle-datalog with displayed == executed.
- Attach loads advisory guidance as attached pack skill context; attach does not execute rules.
- Rule-pack run applies what the pack can do: deterministic evaluation of promoted rules when present; advisory-only walkthrough when no rules; mixed packs may do both; guidance never mints engine verdicts.
- Explicit per-clause promote creates a draft rule; LLM-assisted drafting is allowed only inside the expressible predicate island (topology/reachability, component/class presence, source numeric attribute comparisons against thresholds).
- Outside the island, promotion abstains and the clause remains advisory; grow the island on demand from recurring grounded abstentions—not via an ambitious EPA/HAZOP compiler.
- Introduce a rule outcome convention: fixed Souffle relations/evidence schema for satisfied / violated / indeterminate (+ scoped evidence) so one generic runner evaluates any validated fence.
- Generalize the existing pack-rule evaluation entrypoint (today’s bundled evaluator) to that generic runner; migrate the two demo rules onto it; remove dependence on a per-rule_id Python adapter map for new authored rules.
- Authored promoted rules carry author-confirmed rule trust per ADR 0007; never bundled rule-pack trust.
- One Souffle engine remains shared with ad-hoc Datalog per ADR 0008; this PRD does not merge trust tiers.
- OSS v1: no ASP. Session exception facts are optional later crisp encoding for waivers/exceptions, not part of the vertical-slice must-have.
- Product completion bar for this PRD: one hybrid pack vertical slice (ingest → attach → promote → generic run → in-thread evidence).
- Primary test seam: generalized pack-rule evaluation entrypoint under the rule outcome convention.
- Supporting seams: markdown parse; review-session rule-pack HTTP surface (ingest/list/load/run/promote).
- Do not make run_grounded_qa_turn the primary seam for this slice; skill-context/walkthrough may integrate there later once attach/run wiring exists.
- No workflow DAG / order-of-execution scheduler for rules in this PRD.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior only: pack parse shape, attach vs run semantics, promote abstain/success, evaluation outcomes/evidence, displayed==executed, and HTTP wiring—not Souffle subprocess internals or private adapter helpers.
- Prefer the highest existing seams: generalized evaluate-pack-rule entrypoint; parse_rule_pack_markdown; review API session rule-pack routes.
- Prior art: tests/verification for bundled/souffle/markdown contracts; tests/web/test_review_api.py for load/run; do not require a new parallel evaluation API if the existing entrypoint can be generalized.
- Keep existing bundled outcome/evidence assertions green after migrating demos onto the generic runner.
- Add tests for: advisory-only markdown ingest and attachability; promote of an in-island clause to a runnable fence; promote abstain outside the island; authored rule execution through the generic runner without a new Python adapter; rule-pack run advisory walkthrough emits no rule evaluation outcomes; mixed pack run returns engine results only for rules.
- Scripted/fake providers for any LLM promote path; assert harness gating and stored artifacts, not live model quality.
- Avoid orchestration-matrix tests (rule order, stage graphs, concurrency of checklist steps).

## Out of Scope

- Bulk auto-compilation of HAZOP/EPA documents into trusted executable rules on upload.
- ASP / full defeasible deontic reasoning engine in OSS v1.
- Elevating authored rules to bundled rule-pack trust or cross-user shared trust.
- Uploading pre-made packs that skip promotion and claim trusted executable status.
- Workflow/DAG order-of-execution infrastructure for advisory checklists.
- Making run_grounded_qa_turn the primary delivery seam for this vertical slice.
- Expanding the expressible predicate island to cover physics correlations or external formulas.
- Implementing session exception facts as a must-have inside this slice (allowed as a later crisp extension).
- Graded accuracy eval claiming measurable HAZOP/EPA compliance improvement.
- Team/org shared authored packs and paid-tier governance sophistication.

## Further Notes

- Grill decisions (2026-07-24): hybrid packs; paste→advisory; OSS v1 markdown ingest allowed; attach→skill context; run=apply-what-pack-can-do; promote only inside expressible island; grow island on demand; rewrite 311; generic rule outcome convention; Datalog+optional later session exception facts (no ASP); done bar = hybrid pack vertical slice.
- Glossary updates landed in CONTEXT.md for advisory pack guidance, attached pack skill context, markdown pack ingest, expressible predicate island, rule outcome convention, hybrid pack vertical slice, session exception fact, and related revisions.
- ADR 0013 records the hybrid advisory-vs-executable trust split and supersedes bead 311’s compile-on-upload contract.
- Related: pydexpi-datalog-1-2yr (interactive authoring / first-confirmation trust), pydexpi-datalog-1-2c5.4 (attach modal), pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (Souffle execution PRD—partially stale vs current demo Souffle path), pydexpi-datalog-1-rmso.3 (defeasible/deontic characterization—feeds later exception-fact/ASP decisions, not this slice).

title: Hosted accounts database on shared libSQL, not instance disk
description:
The hosted profile's accounts database is a better-sqlite3 file on the instance. frontend/lib/auth.ts constructs Better Auth with 'database: new Database(authDatabasePath())' in every profile; PYDEXPI_AUTH_DB changes the path, not the driver.

Two consequences, both the exact failure ADR 0016 set out to remove:
1. A second instance has its own user table. An account created on instance A does not exist on instance B.
2. Better Auth's jwt plugin persists its JWKS signing keys in that same database (node_modules/better-auth/dist/plugins/jwt/schema.mjs). The Python backend fetches JWKS from $BETTER_AUTH_URL/api/auth/jwks, which behind a load balancer resolves to an arbitrary instance, so a token signed by A fails verification against B's keys. This fails intermittently rather than cleanly.
3. A redeploy discards every account and every signing key.

Beads 2afe.6 through 2afe.9 moved the Python backend's state (sessions, artifacts, provider keys) onto shared services. The accounts database was never in that scope and the gap went unnamed until after the epic's children were closed. Until this lands, hosted is single-instance-with-a-volume, not horizontally scalable. README and ADR 0016 now say so explicitly.

What to build: point Better Auth at the same libSQL database the session catalog uses. libSQL is SQLite's dialect, and Better Auth accepts a Kysely dialect, so this should be a driver swap rather than a schema rewrite - which is what lib/auth.ts's own comment anticipated. Verify against a real libsql-server, not a file.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] The hosted profile stores accounts in the shared database, not on instance disk
- [ ] Two app instances against one database see the same users
- [ ] A token signed by one instance verifies against the other's JWKS
- [ ] Accounts and signing keys survive replacing the container
- [ ] The local profile still creates no accounts database at all
- [ ] scripts/migrate-auth.mjs migrates the shared database
- [ ] A hosted instance refuses to start on an instance-local accounts file
notes: 2026-07-28 correction: reopened immediately. This is distinct from 2afe.7: 1pqj owns Better Auth account/JWKS shared persistence and cross-instance token verification; 2afe.7 owns the Python review-session catalog. The audit incorrectly classified them as duplicates.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Architecture reconciliation recommendation — 2026-07-28

**Authority:** Harvey-style doctrine map `3ebh`, especially corpus decision `.1`, answer-posture decision `.2`, document-analysis decision `.3`, and curated-skill decision `.5`; deployment ADR 0016; measured latency epic `2bla`. This is a recommendation only: no child ticket is closed by this audit.

### A. Close / supersede: contradicts the new doctrine

1. `1nox` and children `.1`–`.6` — user-uploaded hybrid Markdown packs, agent-guidance attach, per-clause promotion, and authored generic execution. Doctrine `.5` makes guidance **operator-managed curated skills**, not an ordinary engineer upload/authoring surface. Skills may not activate/execute Verify rules. Preserve only the generic deterministic-runner lessons as implementation reference, not the product PRD.
2. `2yr` and children `.1`–`.3` — interactive personal authored rules, confirmation, and authored-pack browse/attach. Same contradiction; reusable rule authoring is outside the doctrine horizon.
3. `37l3` — persisted multi-document topology collection. Doctrine `.1` keeps one DEXPI spine; attachments are chat-scoped and do not form a multi-document/fused topology collection.
4. `2c5.5`, `.6`, `.7` — projects/nested-chat tree, multi-diagram attachment, and fan-out QA. Superseded by one-file DEXPI review scope plus chat-scoped attachments and explicit, later document analysis; no multi-spine/fan-out review loop.
5. `3qo.9` and its `.1`–`.16` implementation programme — automatic template/generated-Datalog execution and automatic generated fallback contradicts `.2`: Inspect auto-routes; Verify only starts when explicitly invoked, with explicit validated rule-pack selection and deterministic evidence. Its route-receipt/fidelity research remains background reference for `rmso`, not an active product PRD.
6. `3qo` — broad model-assisted temporary-logic PRD is superseded as product scope by explicit-posture doctrine.
7. `37x.21.7` — stopped/abandoned query-scope removal; the current source-spine and explicit mode contracts replace its premise.
8. `1pqj` — duplicate of deployment epic child `2afe.7` (shared libSQL hosted catalog), so retain the parent child only.

### B. Rewrite before any implementation: retain the valuable boundary, discard old product shape

1. `2afe` and `.11` — retain durable local/hosted artifacts, catalog, Principal, and BYOK. Rewrite chats as an independent durable `chat_id` with ordered messages, chat-scoped attachments, and links to one-or-more **independent** source sessions; remove project-as-corpus language. `.11` remains P0 but paused until rewritten.
2. `2c5` — do not implement the current epic. Salvage only inspectable review-surface primitives (routed navigation, resizable panes, zoom/pan) later under an evidence-on-drawing/review-surface ticket. Remove projects, multi-diagram fan-out, rule-pack browsing/attach UX, and user-authored-pack assumptions.
3. `2ki` — keep the drawing-faithful renderer and evidence-on-drawing ambitions; rewrite its calm shell/turn presentation around Inspect / explicit Verify / explicit Propose disclosures, document claims, reconciliation, and non-applying patches. Remove normal-user rule-pack picker and stale confirmation-centric stepping.
4. `37x` / `37x.22` — keep the single-file web review seam, grounded evidence, witnesses, direction honesty, and conversation substrate; rewrite all autogenerated/ad-hoc-logic and old confirmation language to the answer-posture contract.
5. `37x.22.34` — retain real Soufflé and resource-bound deterministic execution as foundation; split/retire model-authored ad-hoc Datalog and its confirmation widget. Verify becomes explicit selection of a maintained/validated executable rule/check, not implicit conversational escalation.
6. `xzpx` — too broad to act on. Replace with individual currently reproducible test-failure beads after re-baselining; do not treat it as an implementation work item.

### C. Keep: architecture-aligned foundations, evidence, or isolated defects

- `rmso`, `.3`, `.6`, `3q1`, `8g2i`: the separate proof/evaluation research spine. Do not merge it into the doctrine map; its outputs may later inform explicit Verify.
- `2bla` and `.2`–`.5.3`: latency/caching/streaming/ARM work. Keep, but prioritize only after measured workloads establish the bottleneck; it is not justification for a desktop rewrite.
- `2afe.1`–`.10` except `.11`: local/hosted deployment seams, artifact/catalog/auth/BYOK work remain valid, subject to the chat rewrite above. `1iep`, `23bx` remain deferred deployment/auth work.
- `37x.18`: full review-workflow smoke remains valuable once its asserted flow matches the rewritten posture UX.
- `37zz`, `bjya`, `hawf`: Soufflé correctness/resources/CI; retain. `hawf` remains blocked until its live-suite nondeterminism is resolved.
- `1m6`, `1z2`, `3oo1`, `3tt`, `swe`: isolated frontend/test/formatting defects. Retain, but investigate whether `1m6` + `1z2` are one root cause and update `swe` against the current intended direction-review contract.
- `37x.21.12`: park as fog; GraphML is not an active interchange requirement.

### Required reconciliation sequence (one ticket resolution per session)

1. Close the duplicate `1pqj` with duplicate-of-`2afe.7` rationale.
2. Close the clear hybrid-authoring family (`1nox`, then its children as policy permits) with doctrine `.5` rationale.
3. Close the interactive-authoring family (`2yr` children) with the same rationale.
4. Close multi-spine/fan-out tickets (`37l3`, `2c5.5`–`.7`).
5. Supersede old automatic logic PRDs (`3qo.9`, then `3qo`) while leaving `rmso` intact.
6. Rewrite the retained parent tickets (`2afe`, `2ki`, `37x.22`, `37x.22.34`) before resuming their children.

title: Resolve source-rooted queries by deterministic object selectors
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-153 PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer

## What to build

Make source-rooted deterministic QA queries usable without requiring users to know internal graph node IDs. The query command should accept deterministic object selectors and resolve them through Datalog facts/predicates from the combined derived graph semantics artifact.

Allowed source selectors:

- --source-id for exact/debug/test use
- --source-tag for human-facing equipment tags such as P-4713
- --source-proteus-id for source Proteus IDs such as CentrifugalPump-1

Do not add --source-label. Class labels are too loose and commonly non-unique.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] query-derived-graph accepts --source-tag and --source-proteus-id for source-rooted supported queries.
- [ ] --source-id remains supported for exact tests and debugging.
- [ ] Source selector resolution uses Datalog output from the combined artifact, not Python parsing of graph_facts.json.
- [ ] Source-rooted supported queries fail clearly if no source selector is provided.
- [ ] If multiple selectors are provided and resolve to the same node, the query succeeds and records the resolved source ID.
- [ ] If multiple selectors resolve to different nodes, the query fails with a structured diagnostic.
- [ ] If a selector matches no node, the query fails with a structured diagnostic.
- [ ] If a selector matches multiple nodes, the query fails with an ambiguity diagnostic.
- [ ] Query corpus entries for compare_known_object_reachability and compare_direct_process_connections mark source selection as source-rooted.

## Notes

This bead should not add source-label selection and should not default source-rooted queries to the first graph node.

title: Evaluate desktop shell and Pi integration options
description: Evaluate, do not assume, whether PortLog should add a desktop shell and whether Pi components are useful. Compare: (1) browser/hosted client, (2) a thin Electron shell supervising the existing local Python+Souffle sidecar, and (3) Pi package integration limited to optional auth/agent-adapter capabilities. PortLog ArtifactStore, SessionCatalog, TurnLifecycleStore, review API, and Python+Souffle execution remain authoritative in every option. Prove local-versus-hosted Pi OAuth feasibility before any adoption recommendation. Do not fork pi-gui or use Pi JSONL sessions as review state.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Proposed evaluation plan

### Hypothesis
A thin Electron shell plus an optional Pi SDK adapter can make local PortLog feel like a cohesive engineering review workstation without moving product authority out of PortLog.

### Deep-module seams to prove
1. **Local review runtime module** — small interface: start, health, stop, endpoint. Electron main is one adapter that supervises the existing Python review API + Souffle process; hosted web is another adapter that supplies a remote endpoint. ArtifactStore, SessionCatalog, TurnLifecycleStore, and the review API remain behind this seam.
2. **Agent-provider module** — small interface: run a governed PortLog turn against approved tool receipts and return typed turn events. Current provider path and an optional Pi SDK adapter satisfy it. Pi SessionManager/JSONL are never the review-session authority.
3. **Credential module** — small interface: acquire/use/forget a provider credential for a selected deployment profile. Spike Pi OAuth via local loopback/paste-back and determine whether browser-hosted reuse is technically/legal/UX viable.

### Ordered spikes
A. **Electron runtime spike:** wrap the existing frontend; Electron main starts/stops a local Python+Souffle sidecar, passes only a loopback endpoint, waits for health, shows crash/restart diagnostics, and shuts down cleanly. Prove macOS first; write the concrete Linux/Windows packaging gaps rather than assuming portability.
B. **Pi SDK adapter spike:** use `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` from the Electron main/sidecar process to run one scripted provider turn through PortLog’s existing governed tool/evidence route. Prove that PortLog remains the authority for turn IDs, artifacts, evidence, and cancellation.
C. **OAuth/profile spike:** test Pi login/auth storage only for a local desktop profile first; then assess hosted/browser use separately. Record subscription/extra-usage economics and never copy `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` into PortLog storage by default.
D. **Workflow comparison:** put one actual review journey side-by-side (open DEXPI, inspect drawing/evidence, attach supporting document, invoke Verify, inspect witness/result) and identify whether desktop changes capability, latency, or merely chrome.

### Decision gates
Recommend Electron + Pi only if A–C preserve PortLog authority, do not introduce a second persisted session model, have a credible packaging/security path, and D produces a material review-workflow gain. Otherwise choose Electron without Pi, web without Electron, or defer both. No production shell migration, pi-gui fork, or auth adoption occurs during this evaluation.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Initial spike evidence — 2026-07-28

### Electron local-runtime seam
- Added an evaluation-only `frontend/desktop/local-review-runtime.ts` module. Its public contract starts a loopback child only after health responds, forwards a local deployment environment overlay, and terminates/awaits a silent child that misses the one startup deadline.
- Added three Node behavior tests. They pass.
- Electron `43.2.0` installs and launches on this macOS machine. A minimal launcher is deliberately sandboxed (`contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`) and fails closed when no UI endpoint is configured. It is not yet a sidecar-integrated desktop product.

### Pi SDK
- Initial install of `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent@0.73.1` emitted deprecation warnings directing consumers to `@earendil-works/*`; removed it.
- Installed maintained `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.82.1`, Node >=22.19. Its real `createAgentSession`, `SessionManager`, and `ModelRegistry` exports load under the PortLog frontend runtime.
- No OAuth, Pi session persistence, or governed Pi-backed turn has been adopted/proven yet.

### Next evidence needed
1. Start the actual local PortLog Python review API through the supervisor and prove health/clean stop.
2. Launch Electron against a live PortLog frontend and inspect one real review workflow.
3. Build a one-turn Pi adapter proof that preserves PortLog authority for turn/artifact/evidence/cancellation IDs.
4. Perform the local Pi OAuth feasibility test; hosted/browser remains a separate experiment.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Second spike evidence — actual PortLog sidecar

- Added a cross-stack integration test that launches the real local `pydexpi_datalog.web.asgi:app` Uvicorn process through the desktop supervisor, waits for `/api/review/sessions`, observes `200 {"sessions": []}`, then cleanly stops it and removes its temporary artifact root. It passes.
- Uvicorn publishes its readiness line on standard error in this environment, not guaranteed standard output. The supervisor now observes both streams, still under one startup deadline and cleanup path.
- Pi SDK construction interface confirms the needed safety seam: `createAgentSession` supports `noTools: "all"`, an explicit tool allowlist, `customTools`, and `SessionManager.inMemory()`. A PortLog Pi adapter must use those controls; it must never enable Pi built-in read/bash/edit/write tools or let Pi persist its JSONL session as PortLog review state.

Electron itself is still only a secure dev launcher; live-window workflow and packaging are not yet proven. Pi OAuth and a real governed Pi-backed provider turn remain unproven.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Active acceptance plan — 2026-07-28

Feasibility setup is not the decision outcome. The bead remains in progress until it has: (1) an Electron-rendered journey against the actual local PortLog API and Next frontend that prepares and displays a real DEXPI review; (2) a Pi-backed governed-turn proof with Pi built-ins disabled, PortLog-owned IDs/evidence/artifacts, and observable cancellation; (3) a local OAuth feasibility result plus a separately documented hosted/browser assessment; and (4) an explicit adopt/defer recommendation against the decision gates.

First acceptance journey: local Python review API + local Next frontend + Electron renderer → prepare checked-in DEXPI fixture → observe real prepared review surface, session identity, and drawing/evidence UI.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Governed Pi adapter spike — 2026-07-28

- Added a real in-memory Pi turn adapter: it uses an explicit `models.json` runtime, `SessionManager.inMemory`, and an allowlist containing only `portlog_evidence`; Pi JSONL persistence and all built-in tools are excluded.
- Behavioral contract uses a local fake OpenAI-compatible model that requests `portlog_evidence`; it proves only that PortLog tool is exposed, calls the caller-owned evidence resolver, carries the caller AbortSignal, and completes the model/tool cycle.
- Evidence ownership remains outside Pi. This is an adapter feasibility proof, not product wiring.
- Validation: `node --experimental-strip-types --test desktop/pi-turn-adapter.test.ts` and `npm run typecheck` pass. `npm run lint` remains blocked by pre-existing formatting drift across 49 unrelated files (plus an existing unused parameter warning).

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text: Follow-up: strengthened the behavioral contract so the caller aborts while the governed evidence resolver is executing. The resolver observes the same AbortSignal as aborted, and Pi makes no follow-on model request. This proves caller-owned cancellation reaches the PortLog tool boundary and stops the Pi turn.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## OAuth feasibility assessment — 2026-07-28

**Local Electron: feasible, but not yet product-wired.** Pi’s Anthropic Pro/Max OAuth implementation is Node-only, opens a loopback callback server on `127.0.0.1:53692`, and has a UI-neutral manual redirect/code fallback. That fits Electron **main process** supervision; it does not fit the sandboxed renderer. Pi persists refresh/access tokens in `auth.json` by default, so PortLog must inject a credential store backed by Electron `safeStorage`/OS keychain before exposing Login.

**Hosted/browser: defer.** The same implementation explicitly says it is Node/CLI-only. A hosted backend’s loopback callback would be on the server—not the reviewer’s machine—and accepting a pasted user redirect would transfer a subscription token to PortLog’s backend. That crosses the BYOK credential boundary and needs a separately designed browser OAuth flow, consent model, encrypted server store, and provider terms review. No credential reuse claim is justified.

**Recommendation:** prove a local main-process Login spike before enabling it; keep hosted BYOK API-key-only for this evaluation. Pi OAuth is a local optional capability, never PortLog review state.

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Evaluation decision — 2026-07-28

**Adopt Electron as the local desktop shell; adopt Pi only as an optional, governed per-turn adapter. Do not adopt pi-gui as a base.**

Evidence: (1) Electron rendered the real local PortLog review journey—upload checked-in DEXPI, prepare, then draw topology and schematic—against the actual local FastAPI and Next stack. (2) The Pi adapter completes a real model/tool cycle with only the PortLog evidence tool, in-memory session state, and caller-owned cancellation. (3) pi-gui’s JSONL session authority and packaging model remain incompatible with PortLog’s artifact/catalog/turn source of truth.

**Implementation boundary:** Electron main process supervises the existing local Python + Soufflé review API; the renderer loads the existing Next client; PortLog’s ArtifactStore, SessionCatalog, TurnLifecycleStore, review API, and deterministic evidence remain authoritative. Pi never owns review IDs, artifacts, evidence, or cancellation.

**Deferred gates:** package/sign the Python+Soufflé sidecar for macOS first; run a local Electron-main OAuth Login proof using secure OS credential storage; assess hosted/browser OAuth separately. UI redesign and Pi-powered product turns wait for those gates.

title: Add whole-P&ID query mode without first-node defaults
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-153 PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer

## What to build

Add query corpus and harness support for whole-P&ID deterministic queries that evaluate across the complete P&ID instead of treating an arbitrary graph node as a root.

Do not default source-rooted queries to the first node in the graph. NetworkX insertion order and container-like nodes such as ConceptualModel are not meaningful engineering defaults.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Query corpus metadata can distinguish source-rooted queries from whole_pid queries.
- [ ] Whole-P&ID queries run without requiring --source-id, --source-tag, or --source-proteus-id.
- [ ] Source-rooted queries still require an explicit source selector.
- [ ] The query harness rejects accidental first-node default behavior.
- [ ] A first whole-P&ID query entry exists in the corpus, focused on a realistic P&ID-wide question rather than generic reachability.
- [ ] Whole-P&ID query artifacts record that the scope was the whole P&ID, not a selected source node.
- [ ] Tests prove a whole-P&ID query can run or return a structured unsupported/future-candidate artifact without a source selector.

## Notes

This is likely the precursor to all-pump discharge-path classification. Keep it separate from source selector work so source-rooted and whole-P&ID query semantics remain explicit.
close_reason: Implemented whole-P&ID query scope metadata and future-candidate query artifacts without source selector defaults. Validation: .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests (84 tests OK).

title: Emit human-readable node alias facts in derived graph semantics
description:

Context:

- Emit node_proteus_id(id, proteus_id) facts from node attribute proteusId when present.
- Consider emitting node_display_name(id, display) with a narrow deterministic fallback order: tagName, then proteusId, then label.
- Do not replace node_id in existing predicates.

title: get_reachable_equipment reports isolation for nozzle-connected equipment
description: Observed live in the prototype REPL on E06 ('Pump, HeatExchanger, Nozzles Connected With PNS'): asked which equipment is not connected to piping, the model called get_reachable_equipment for P-4713 and H-1009, got reachable=[] with outcome=violated and coverage.complete=true, and faithfully answered that BOTH equipment items are isolated from piping -- with validated citations and no disclosure. This directly contradicts the deterministic bundled-template verdict on the same drawing (piping_connected(P-4713,H-1009) holds; no_violation). Diagnosis (verified by probing the prepared session): topology_view contains NO equipment<->nozzle edges -- graph_facts has 'CentrifugalPump --nozzles--> Nozzle' edges but the topology view construction drops the 'nozzles' (and 'taggedPlantItems') relationships, so traversal from an equipment node finds zero edges and reports complete coverage of an empty frontier. Every DEXPI drawing where equipment connects through nozzles (i.e. all of them) makes this tool claim total isolation. Fix should make get_reachable_equipment traverse the equipment->nozzle association (from graph_facts or by including the edge in topology_view) and add a regression on the real E06 fixture asserting P-4713 reaches H-1009. Coverage/limitations fields must stop claiming complete=true when the start node has no edges but owns nozzles.
notes: Follow-up required: process-piping traversal now reaches nozzle edges, but the review topology must materialize the same edges so returned witness IDs are highlightable. Reopened to add and validate that rendering contract.
close_reason: Completed follow-up: review topology now materializes canonical process-piping edges, so every E06 P-4713-to-H-1009 witness ID is present in evidence_map and highlightable. Focused semantic/API modules pass (20 tests).

title: Choose PortLog’s reusable isolated Pi runtime architecture
description:
## Destination

Produce a prototype-backed recommendation for PortLog's whole Electron agent runtime architecture on packaged macOS Apple Silicon, including the reuse level for Pi/OMP/VMPI/Gondolin and a coarse adoption outline.

## Notes

- Electron is the sole product surface. The React/Next-derived renderer and loopback Python sidecar are internal Electron modules/adapters, not standalone browser or public backend products.
- Retain local sidecar implementations actually invoked by Electron even when they live under web-named modules or use HTTP.
- Renderer localStorage for selected-provider and shared session/thread state remains internal non-secret UI state; active-turn recovery is part of the excluded legacy non-desktop path.
- Browser BYOK, Better Auth/JWT, hosted accounts/provider-key stores, hosted S3/libSQL/ProfileBundle parity, public Next routes, and public TurnLifecycleStore/HTTP contracts are not target compatibility requirements.
- Planning map; prototypes are evidence for decisions, not production implementation.
- Consult codebase-design, domain-modeling, grilling, research, and prototype as applicable.
- Upstream-first reuse: use unchanged first, then contribute upstream, then add a thin adapter; fork or replace only with documented blocking evidence.
- Compare host-held and guest-scoped credential models empirically.
- The evidence bar is one representative end-to-end engineering review, not a broad benchmark.
- Refer to tickets by title in human-facing map updates.

## Decisions so far

- **Map the current PortLog agent runtime and replacement seam** — Electron is the only product surface, and RunLocalReviewInspectionOptions.createTurn is the narrowest current candidate/internal seam. Preserve the current split: Electron main composes, resolves credentials, creates manifests, and supervises workers; the worker constructs bounded callbacks; the loopback sidecar/flow implements domain operations and persists result artifacts; runLocalReviewInspection mediates callbacks and owns normalized inspection events/records, posture, terminal and cancellation/error mapping, and inspection-turn upsert requests; the manifest module performs the writes. Evidence: docs/research/pydexpi-datalog-1-23bh.1-current-runtime-seam.md.
- **Inventory reusable Pi, OMP, VMPI, and Gondolin capabilities** — Reuse exact Pi core+AI 0.80.6 unchanged behind the existing PortLog adapter; treat OMP as interface evidence rather than a product shell; run unmodified VMPI 0.4.1 only as the .5 prototype because macOS/aarch64 are upstream-untested; evaluate Gondolin VM/VFS/network/lifecycle implementations only behind a thin PortLog adapter. No fork/replace or final topology decision is justified yet. Evidence: docs/research/pydexpi-datalog-1-23bh.2-upstream-capability-inventory.md.
- **Define the representative end-to-end review scenario** — Compare Hybrid (host Pi and PortLog operations; guest risky command) with Full guest (guest Pi and risky command; host-authorized PortLog capabilities) using the same immutable E06 bundle, governed pump check, bounded command artifact, six confinement probes, stable-phase cancellation, and cold retry. Guest input is read-only, scratch is ephemeral, and a guest-readable provider credential is a failure; missing mediation remains blocked evidence rather than an assumed pass. Evidence: docs/research/pydexpi-datalog-1-23bh.4-representative-review-scenario.md.

## Not yet specified

- Any concrete upstream contribution or additional thin adapter justified by executable VMPI/Gondolin and topology evidence.
- Final guest networking, mount, checkpoint, and artifact-retention policy after the runtime topology is selected.
- The precise structured Electron event bridge and PortLog-native tool transport after the viable integration path is demonstrated.

## Out of scope

- Production implementation and detailed migration backlog.
- Deleting obsolete browser/hosted code without a separately authorized cleanup bead.
- A broad actor-unaware capability benchmark; this map uses one representative review.
- Redesigning PortLog's evidence ontology or grounded-verdict doctrine.
- Reimplementing existing Pi, OMP, VMPI, Gondolin, or document-tool capabilities without demonstrated blockers.
notes: Completed architecture map: adopt Hybrid host Pi plus disposable Gondolin isolated-command guests. Reuse Pi core+AI unchanged; Gondolin upstream directly; OMP as design evidence; VMPI as prototype evidence only. Prototype krun first for packaging, retain QEMU/HVF as measured reference, and fail closed. Adopt through an optional worker-supplied command callback in the existing host Pi adapter, disabled by default, with no createTurn change, host fallback, dual execution, project migration, or guest persistence. Promote only after full confinement, lifecycle, signed/notarized clean-machine, compatibility, and rollback gates. Evidence: docs/research/pydexpi-datalog-1-23bh.7-runtime-architecture-decision.md and docs/research/pydexpi-datalog-1-23bh.8-reversible-adoption-outline.md.
close_reason: Completed prototype-backed Electron isolated runtime architecture and reversible adoption recommendation

title: Qualify packaged macOS virtualization constraints
description:
## Question

What packaging, signing, notarization, entitlement, redistribution, architecture, installation, and runtime constraints govern shipping VMPI/Gondolin/QEMU inside the Apple Silicon PortLog desktop application?
notes: Research complete. Shipping an arm64 VM substrate in directly distributed PortLog is feasible in principle, but current packaging is not production-eligible: ad-hoc identity, hardened runtime off, strict verification off, and sidecar signing exclusions block notarized distribution. QEMU is technically plausible but has a large relocatable dylib/resource and GPL compliance burden. Gondolin's compact Darwin-arm64 krun runner is the preferred packaged experiment, but remains experimental and unproven under Developer ID signing/notarization; it still requires per-executable hypervisor entitlement, signed dylibs, boot assets, clean-machine proof, and license/source compliance. Evidence: docs/research/pydexpi-datalog-1-23bh.3-macos-virtualization-constraints.md

title: Run the unmodified VMPI Apple Silicon review prototype
description:
## Question

title: PRD: Local and hosted deployment profiles — per-user persistence of files and chats
description:
## Problem Statement

Review artifacts are written to a filesystem tree keyed by a session id that is minted as a random UUID in browser localStorage. Nothing indexes that tree, so clearing browser storage orphans a session's artifacts on disk with nothing left that can name them. A local operator loses files exactly the way a hosted user would. There is no user, no catalog, and no database anywhere in the repository, and AuthoredRulePackStore writes to a single global directory shared by every session, which already violates the authored rule pack and author-confirmed rule trust definitions.

## Solution

Ship two deployment profiles from one codebase per ADR 0016. The local profile keeps every artifact on the operator's own machine with no accounts and no network services. The hosted profile persists per-user projects, chats, and review sessions behind sign-in. The profile is selected once at the composition root and is invisible below it. Three seams carry the difference: Principal (constant workspace locally, authenticated subject hosted), ArtifactStore (filesystem locally, object storage hosted), and Catalog (SQLite locally, libSQL hosted, one dialect and one migration set).

The catalog exists in both profiles because the problem it solves is findability, not durability. The first three slices ship real value with no auth, no hosting, and no cloud account: a local operator stops losing files.

## Governing ADR

docs/adr/0016-local-and-hosted-deployment-profiles.md

title: Reword profile-dependent glossary terms for both deployment profiles
description:
## Parent

title: Persist per-chat messages and attachments server-side
description: Observed in the hosted Oracle deployment: chat history is not durable. New chat clears the only history; reopening a catalog session cannot restore its own messages; another browser cannot recover them. title: Principal seam and workspace-scoped artifact root
description:
## Parent
pydexpi-datalog-1-2afe

## What to build
Introduce a Principal that resolves a user identity and a workspace scoping key, and scope every artifact path by that workspace. The local resolver returns a constant, so a single operator sees no behavioural change. This is the prefactor the rest of the epic builds on, and it fixes the authored rule pack leak: authored packs are written to one global directory shared by every session today, which violates the authored rule pack and author-confirmed rule trust definitions that scope packs to a single user.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A Principal exposing a user identity and a workspace key is resolved at the composition root
- [ ] Uploads, exports, session artifacts, and authored rule packs are all written beneath the workspace
- [ ] Two workspaces cannot see each other's sessions or authored rule packs
- [ ] Author-confirmed rule trust granted in one workspace does not apply in another
- [ ] Existing behaviour for a single local operator is unchanged and the existing suite passes

None — can start immediately
