title: Persist Datalog approval audit record at execution time
description:
## What to build

Record a durable approval artifact each time a temporary Datalog proposal is approved and executed, so there is a replayable audit trail of what ran, against which graph, and when.

## Target

- `pydexpi_datalog/web/chainlit_review_flow.py` — `submit_temporary_datalog_review`
- `pydexpi_datalog/qa/topology_tools.py` — `execute_confirmed_temporary_datalog`
- New file: `pydexpi_datalog/qa/datalog_audit.py` (or alongside `topology_tools.py`)

## Change

After successful execution, persist an approval record containing:

```json
{
  "proposal_id": "<sha256-prefix>",
  "session_id": "...",
  "question": "...",
  "formal_restatement": "...",
  "generated_datalog": "...",
  "decision": "approved",
  "decided_at": "<ISO-8601>",
  "executed": true,
  "execution_status": "answered" | "execution_failed"
}
```

Write to a per-session JSONL file (e.g. `.tmp/review-sessions/{session_id}/datalog_audit.jsonl`) so records survive process restart and are independently readable.

Cancel decisions should also be recorded (`decision: canceled, executed: false`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every confirm-and-run decision appends a record to the session audit log before returning the result.
- [ ] Every cancel decision appends a record with `executed: false`.
- [ ] The audit record includes `proposal_id`, `session_id`, `question`, `formal_restatement`, `generated_datalog`, `decision`, `decided_at`, `executed`, `execution_status`.
- [ ] A unit test reads the audit log after a confirm and a cancel and asserts the expected fields.
close_reason: Confirm and cancel decisions append JSONL audit records to {artifact_root}/{session_id}/datalog_audit.jsonl via pydexpi_datalog/qa/datalog_audit.py, wired into submit_temporary_datalog_review before each return (commit 7f05ae0). Hardened by f8a249c: approvals now execute only server-stored proposals, and audit records for unknown/forged proposals record executed=false. Unit test reads the log after confirm and cancel and asserts all required fields. Backend 177/177 green.

title: PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog
description:
## Problem Statement

The repository's logic-programming story is built but not wired in. The pyDEXPI full graph is
exported into a real Souffle EDB, and a real generic-graph IDB schema
(`graph_topology_semantics.dl`) declares reusable traversal predicates — but nothing actually
executes them. Rule-pack evaluation (the `pump_discharge_check_valve` demo rule) is hand-written
Python graph traversal explicitly labeled `python_traversal`, not a logic program, despite being
presented to users as a "rule pack." The QA chat's `propose_temporary_datalog` capability — the
model's only escape hatch when read-only retrieval tools are insufficient — is a two-shape regex
shim that silently returns zero evidence for any generated Datalog beyond two exact recognized
shapes, with no error, which is worse than a rejection because it looks like "no matching
objects" instead of "this feature doesn't run your query." And even when the model does select
`propose_temporary_datalog`, there is no mid-turn mechanism connecting it to the
`generated-Datalog confirmation gate` that the frontend already renders elsewhere in the product
— the tool call is treated as satisfying the model's intent and the turn completes, meaning the
capability is a dead end in live usage today.

Process engineers cannot yet get a HAZOP-style answer (e.g. "do all pumps have isolation valves,
a check valve, and a strainer?") that is actually backed by deterministic logic execution, because
no real Souffle program runs for either the trusted rule-pack path or the model-drafted ad-hoc
path. The product's core differentiating bet — LLM drafts, deterministic logic engine verifies —
is not yet true anywhere except a narrow, single-purpose source-resolution lookup in
`source_selection.py`.

## Solution

Wire one real Souffle execution engine to serve both existing trust tiers, without merging them:

- **Bundled rule-pack trust** (repository-reviewed, e.g. `pump_discharge_check_valve`) keeps
  running immediately with no confirmation gate, but its `executable_logic` becomes a real
  Souffle program over the shared EDB/IDB schema instead of Python traversal.
- **Model-drafted ad-hoc Datalog** (`propose_temporary_datalog`) stays behind the mandatory
  `generated-Datalog confirmation gate` regardless of whether the drafted query is read-only —
  the trust axis here is reviewed-vs-unreviewed authorship, not read/write. This capability is
  wired into the `TurnLifecycleStore` pause/resume mechanism that already exists (built for a
  different, non-conversational Datalog review flow) and already has a working confirmation-card
  UI in the assistant thread — this session reuses that infrastructure rather than building new
  HITL plumbing.

To make ad-hoc queries actually useful once they execute for real, the `predicate contract`
handed to the model expands from the current two-name allowlist (`answer`, `reachable`) to the
real generic `graph_topology_semantics.dl` layer, derived dynamically per session together with
the IDB predicates of whichever rule pack(s) are loaded — read-only for ad-hoc queries, since
rule packs remain the only path that can encode new curated logic.

A typed numeric-attribute predicate is added to the schema so rules and ad-hoc queries can
compare source-provided numeric values (e.g. a pressure rating already present in the DEXPI
source) against thresholds — this does not extend to calculations requiring external formulas or
physical constants not present in the source, which must surface as `source_data_unavailable`
rather than being computed inside a rule.

Finally, a universal claim over multiple objects (e.g. "do all pumps have X, Y, and Z") can
surface more than one pending `direction review` in a single evaluation — one per object whose
flow direction is inferred rather than explicit. The existing pause/resume schema only carries a
single review item per pause; it is extended to carry a list, and the confirmation UI renders all
pending items in one batched card instead of pausing once per item.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want a repository-bundled rule (like pump discharge check valve) to
   actually execute as a real logic program against the loaded source, so that "rule pack" means
   what it says instead of hidden Python traversal.
2. As a process engineer, I want the same rule-evaluation contract (satisfied/violated/
   indeterminate, evidence, scope-completeness) to hold whether the rule runs as Python or
   Souffle, so that existing evidence presentation and testing keep working unchanged.
3. As a process engineer, I want to ask a formal or recursive question in the chat and have the
   model's drafted Datalog actually execute once I approve it, so that `propose_temporary_datalog`
   is a real capability instead of a dead end.
4. As a process engineer, I want every model-drafted query to require my explicit confirmation
   before it runs, regardless of whether it's read-only, so that generated logic never executes
   silently and I retain the same trust guarantee the product has always promised.
5. As a process engineer, I want the confirmation card for a drafted query to show plain-language
   meaning and scope first, with the generated Datalog collapsed but inspectable, so that I can
   approve intended semantics without reading code first.
6. As a process engineer, I want to see a clear, specific error when a drafted query is invalid
   or unsafe, so that "no evidence found" never silently means "this feature is broken."
7. As a process engineer, I want a drafted query to be able to reference the same predicate
   vocabulary a bundled rule pack uses (read-only), so that ad-hoc questions can build on existing
   curated logic instead of starting from a two-predicate allowlist.
8. As a process engineer, I want a drafted query to be validated against a real, complete
   predicate contract rather than a hardcoded two-name allowlist, so that recursion, joins, and
   real constraints actually work instead of silently returning nothing.
9. As a process engineer, I want to compare an actual numeric value already present in the source
   (e.g. a pressure rating) against a threshold in a rule or drafted query, so that HAZOP-style
   quantitative checks are possible without inventing data.
10. As a process engineer, I want a rule or query that needs data or formulas not present in the
    source to say so explicitly, so that missing engineering inputs are never silently assumed or
    invented.
11. As a process engineer, I want to ask a universal question about many objects at once (e.g.
    "do all pumps have an isolation valve, a check valve, and a strainer") and get one evaluation
    covering every resolved object, so that I don't have to ask the same question N times.
12. As a process engineer, I want every object in a universal evaluation with an ambiguous
    (inferred) flow direction to be raised for my review together in one place, so that I'm not
    interrupted repeatedly for the same evaluation.
13. As a process engineer, I want to confirm, reverse, or mark unknown each pending direction
    review independently within that one batched card, so that resolving one doesn't force a
    particular answer on the others.
14. As a process engineer, I want an object whose direction I mark unknown to remain
    indeterminate for that claim rather than being silently excluded or guessed, so that
    uncertainty stays visible in the final answer.
15. As a process engineer, I want the final answer to a universal claim to report satisfied,
    violated, and indeterminate objects individually with their own evidence, so that "mostly
    fine" isn't flattened into a false yes or no.
16. As a process engineer, I want a universal claim to be explicitly disclosed as incomplete when
    my object enumeration itself was truncated, so that partial coverage never quietly reads as a
    complete answer.
17. As a process engineer, I want an off-topic question (e.g. "what model am I talking to") to get
    a brief, honest acknowledgment before being redirected back to P&ID review, so that the
    assistant doesn't feel like it's refusing to talk to me.
18. As a process engineer, I want a follow-up question that refers back to something established
    earlier in the conversation to be answered by reusing that evidence, without the assistant
    needing to redo the same Datalog work, so that conversations stay efficient.
19. As a process engineer, I want any evidence identity cited in an answer — whether newly
    retrieved or reused from earlier in the conversation — to be checked against the current
    topology, so that stale or hallucinated references never pass as evidence.
20. As a developer, I want rule-pack evaluation and ad-hoc query execution to share one real
    Souffle execution path, so that there is exactly one place that runs Datalog and one place to
    harden its safety, timeout, and validation behavior.
21. As a developer, I want the predicate contract exposed to the model to be derived
    programmatically from the EDB/IDB schema and loaded rule-pack declarations, so that it never
    drifts out of sync with the actual schema by hand.
22. As a developer, I want the existing `test_bundled_rule_pack.py` contract tests to continue
    passing unmodified against the Souffle-backed evaluator, so that the migration has a built-in
    regression net instead of needing a parallel test rewrite.
23. As a developer, I want the `TurnLifecycleStore` pause/resume mechanism, already proven for a
    different Datalog-review flow, reused for the QA chat's confirmation gate rather than a new
    mechanism invented, so that pause/resume/cancel semantics stay consistent across the product.
24. As a developer, I want the review-required event payload to support a list of pending items,
    not just one, so that batched direction review has a place to live without a second schema.

## Implementation Decisions

- One real `souffle` execution path serves both repository-bundled rule-pack evaluation and
  model-drafted ad-hoc Datalog (`propose_temporary_datalog`), replacing the current Python
  traversal implementation (`bundled_rule_pack.py`) and the two-shape regex shim
  (`topology_tools.py`'s temporary-Datalog executor) respectively. These remain two separate
  trust tiers on the same engine, not one merged permission model.
- Bundled rule packs keep executing immediately, without a confirmation step, against the full
  EDB/IDB schema (`graph_facts_schema.dl` + `graph_topology_semantics.dl` + rule-pack-specific
  predicates).
- Model-drafted ad-hoc Datalog keeps the mandatory `generated-Datalog confirmation gate`
  regardless of whether the drafted query is read-only. There is no read-only exception — this
  was considered and rejected because the product's actual trust axis is reviewed-vs-unreviewed
  authorship, not read/write.
- `grounded_qa_harness`'s rule-evaluation intent path is wired so that a `propose_temporary_datalog`
  call raises the same `needs_datalog_confirmation` status the `TurnLifecycleStore` already
  supports, pausing the turn instead of treating a `confirmation_required` tool result as
  satisfying the intent and completing the turn.
- The existing confirmation-card UI (assistant thread, Run/Revise/Cancel) is reused for the QA
  chat's confirmation flow rather than building a new HITL surface; this is an integration of
  existing infrastructure into a code path that never used it, not new UI.
- The predicate contract given to the model for `propose_temporary_datalog` is derived
  dynamically per session: the generic `graph_topology_semantics.dl` predicate set, plus the IDB
  predicates declared by whichever rule pack(s) are loaded in that session, exposed read-only.
  Rule-pack predicates are not exposed as a mutable or extensible surface to ad-hoc queries —
  only as join targets.
- A typed numeric-attribute predicate (derived from the existing symbol-typed `node_attribute`
  via Souffle's `to_number()`) is added to the schema so both rule packs and ad-hoc queries can
  perform arithmetic comparisons against source-provided numeric values. Calculations requiring
  external formulas, correlations, or physical constants not present in the source graph remain
  explicitly out of scope and must be reported via the existing `source_data_unavailable`
  grounding posture, never computed inline.
- Object classification for rule logic (e.g. "is this a check valve") uses the existing
  `node_label` predicate, which is already fed from the same source attribute other parts of the
  codebase use as `class_name` — no new fact-export work is required to support type-based
  predicates.
- Universal/absence-style claims over multiple resolved objects (e.g. a "do all pumps have X"
  question) are evaluated as one Datalog program over all resolved identities, not one query per
  object, so the confirmation step itself stays singular even when the claim spans many objects.
- The `TurnLifecycleStore` review-required payload is extended from a single review object to a
  list of pending review items, to support a `direction review` surfacing more than one ambiguous
  object from the same evaluation. The confirmation UI renders all pending items in one card, each
  independently resolvable (confirm/reverse/mark unknown), rather than pausing once per item.
  Marking an item's direction unknown leaves that specific object's outcome `indeterminate` for
  the claim, permanently for that evaluation (not re-askable within it).
- Any evidence reference cited in a final answer — whether obtained via a tool call this turn or
  reused from an earlier turn's `grounded_evidence_ids` — continues to be validated against
  current `known_evidence_ids` before being accepted as grounding; this existing invariant is
  unchanged and is the correct enforcement point for follow-up questions, not a new deterministic
  follow-up classifier.
- The `out_of_scope` grounding-posture policy text is extended to explicitly permit a brief,
  honest acknowledgment of a general/off-topic question before redirecting back to P&ID review,
  instead of implying a bare non-answer. This remains model-owned behavior, not a backend
  classifier, consistent with the existing decision not to build a deterministic intent compiler.
- A prior session handoff's claim that rule-pack verification already runs real recursive Datalog
  is incorrect and is not prior art; see ADR 0008 for the corrected record.

## Testing Decisions

- Test the two existing public seams, not new ones: `run_grounded_qa_turn(...)` in
  `grounded_qa_harness.py` (confirmation-gate wiring, ad-hoc Souffle execution, dynamic predicate
  contract, batched direction review, pause/resume via `TurnLifecycleStore`), and
  `evaluate_bundled_rule(...)` in `bundled_rule_pack.py` (rule-pack Souffle execution, numeric
  attribute comparisons). Prefer these over a new shared seam, since each already has an
  established test suite.
- `tests/verification/test_bundled_rule_pack.py` is prior art and its existing assertions (outcome,
  evidence shape, scope-completeness, direction-review gating) are the regression net for the
  Souffle rewrite — they assert on the public contract, not Python-traversal internals, and should
  continue to pass unmodified.
- `tests/qa/test_grounded_qa_harness.py` and `tests/web/test_turn_lifecycle.py` are prior art for
  pause/resume, confirmation, and round-progress behavior; extend rather than replace.
- Add tests proving `propose_temporary_datalog` confirmation actually pauses the turn
  (`needs_datalog_confirmation`) and that `Run` resumes into real Souffle execution with real
  results, not the two-shape shim's silent-empty behavior.
- Add tests proving invalid or unsafe drafted Datalog produces an explicit validation error, not a
  silent empty result.
- Add tests proving the predicate contract handed to the model reflects the loaded rule pack(s)'
  IDB predicates in addition to the generic schema.
- Add tests proving a numeric-attribute comparison rule correctly classifies satisfied/violated/
  indeterminate outcomes using real source values.
- Add a test proving a universal claim over multiple resolved objects with multiple ambiguous
  directions produces one batched review-required pause listing all pending items, and that each
  item is independently resolvable.
- Add a test proving a follow-up question's cited evidence reference (reused from a prior turn) is
  still validated against current `known_evidence_ids` and rejected if stale/hallucinated.
- Add a test/eval-harness case for the `out_of_scope` acknowledgment-before-redirect behavior,
  as a regression prompt rather than a deterministic assertion on exact wording.
- Avoid asserting on private Souffle subprocess invocation details; assert on the public
  evaluation/execution result contract, matching existing prior art.
- All of the above use scripted fake providers (matching existing prior art like
  `ScriptedQATurnProvider` and the custom fake providers in `test_grounded_qa_harness.py`), not a
  real model — they prove the harness correctly executes, gates, and validates a given tool call,
  not that a real model will choose to draft a correct one.
- Add a minimal live-model verification pass, in the same style used to verify the round-limit fix
  this session (real OpenRouter/BYOK model, live before/after comparison, not just green scripted
  tests): a small, fixed set of real natural-language questions — including at least one
  HAZOP-style universal claim (e.g. "do all pumps have an isolation valve, a check valve, and a
  strainer") and one numeric-threshold question — run against a real tool-calling model, checked
  for a correctly drafted Datalog query, correct confirmation-gate behavior, and a correct final
  outcome. This is not the full graded regression suite against `TrainingTestCases/` (that remains
  separate, out-of-scope future work) — it is a small, manual/scripted proof that the wiring
  produces a correct real answer at least once per capability, not just a proof that scripted
  inputs are handled correctly.

## Out of Scope

- A graded regression eval harness against `TrainingTestCases/` claiming measurable accuracy
  improvement over other tools — tracked separately.
- Replacing the keyword-based intent classifier (`_classify_review_intent`) for initial
  lookup-vs-rule-evaluation routing — remains a pre-retrieval heuristic by design; only
  object-reference disambiguation (via `find_equipment` result counts) is in scope, not intent
  routing.
- Any read-only exception to the `generated-Datalog confirmation gate` — rejected as inconsistent
  with the product's reviewed-vs-unreviewed trust axis.
- Migrating `find_equipment` / `get_reachable_equipment` to Souffle-backed query templates — these
  remain fast, trusted Python/NetworkX lookups; only rule-pack evaluation and ad-hoc generated
  Datalog move to real Souffle execution.
- Supporting calculations that require external formulas, correlations, or physical constants not
  present in the DEXPI source — these must be reported as `source_data_unavailable`, not computed.
- Promoting a user-confirmed ad-hoc query into a reusable rule-pack rule — confirmation remains
  temporary execution consent only, per the existing `Datalog proposal capability` design.
- Rewriting the pause/resume mechanism itself — it already exists and works; this PRD only
  extends its payload shape to support a list of review items and connects the QA chat's
  confirmation-required path into it for the first time.

## Further Notes

This PRD corrects a real misconception surfaced during scoping: the repository's real Souffle
execution today is limited to a single narrow subprocess call in `source_selection.py` for source
resolution. Both the demo rule pack and the QA chat's ad-hoc Datalog capability are currently
non-Datalog stand-ins (Python traversal and a regex shim, respectively), despite being presented
to users as logic-programming capabilities. See `docs/adr/0008-one-souffle-engine-for-rule-packs-and-ad-hoc-queries.md`
for the full architectural decision record, including rejected alternatives.

This work is the direct realization of the product's original bet (LLM drafts, deterministic
Datalog engine verifies) for both the trusted rule-pack path and the conversational ad-hoc path,
and should be treated as foundational rather than incremental — most of the QA chat's
grounding/evidence/confirmation guarantees are currently unproven in practice because nothing
downstream of `propose_temporary_datalog` actually executes.

title: Rule packs run on real Souffle
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Replace the bundled `pump_discharge_check_valve` rule's hand-written Python graph-traversal
implementation with a real `souffle` execution over the existing EDB/IDB schema
(`graph_facts_schema.dl` + `graph_topology_semantics.dl`). This is the first real logic program
in the repository's rule-pack layer; today it is labeled `"language": "python_traversal"` despite
being presented to users as a Datalog rule pack.

Classification predicates for "is this object a check valve" can be built directly from the
existing `node_label(id, label)` predicate, which is already fed from the same source attribute
other parts of the codebase use as `class_name` — no new fact-export work is required.

The public `evaluate_bundled_rule(...)` contract (outcome: satisfied/violated/indeterminate,
evidence shape, `scope_completeness`, direction-basis handling) must not change — this is a swap
of the execution engine underneath an unchanged interface, not a new feature.

Rule packs keep executing immediately with no confirmation gate — this trust tier (repository-
reviewed content) is unaffected by this change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pump_discharge_check_valve` executes as a real Souffle program, not Python traversal.
- [ ] `tests/verification/test_bundled_rule_pack.py` passes unmodified — its existing assertions
      on outcome/evidence/scope-completeness serve as the regression net for this migration.
- [ ] Real fixture graphs already in `testdata/verifier_suite/inputs/` (pass, hard-violation,
      indeterminate cases) are exercised through the new Souffle path, not just synthetic ones.
- [ ] No change to `evaluate_bundled_rule`'s public signature or the shape of its returned
      outcome/evidence dict.
- [ ] No confirmation-gate involvement — this rule continues to execute immediately.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: QA chat confirmation gate wiring, Claude-Code-style inline widget
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Wire the QA chat's `propose_temporary_datalog` capability into the existing
`TurnLifecycleStore` pause/resume mechanism (`needs_datalog_confirmation` status), which today
exists but is never entered from this code path — a `confirmation_required` tool result is
currently treated as satisfying the model's intent, and the turn completes without the query ever
running. This capability is a dead end in live usage until this is fixed.

Render a new, purpose-built confirmation widget inline in the chat thread — a boxed, numbered,
keyboard-navigable choice prompt in the style of Claude Code's interactive tool-approval prompt
(arrow keys / number keys to select, Enter to confirm), not the existing button-based
Run/Revise/Cancel card built for a different, non-conversational Datalog review flow. The widget
shows the plain-language restatement and scope first, with the generated Datalog collapsed but
inspectable, consistent with the product's existing `intent-first confirmation` decision.

No trust escalation: every `propose_temporary_datalog` call requires its own confirmation. There
is no "don't ask again this session" — that was explicitly considered and rejected as
inconsistent with the confirmation gate being temporary execution consent, not reusable-rule
promotion.

This slice does not require the ad-hoc executor to be real Souffle yet (that's the next slice) —
resuming after confirmation may still invoke today's narrow two-shape executor. The point of this
slice is closing the dead end: a user can now actually get to "Run" and receive a result, even a
limited one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `propose_temporary_datalog` call results in the turn pausing with status
      `needs_datalog_confirmation`, not silently completing.
- [ ] The new boxed/numbered/keyboard-navigable widget renders inline in the chat thread showing
      plain-language restatement, scope, and collapsed generated Datalog.
- [ ] Selecting "Run" resumes the turn via `TurnLifecycleStore.resume()` and produces a final
      answer from the (still-current) executor.
- [ ] Selecting "Revise" or "Cancel" produces the same non-executing outcomes the existing
      confirmation flow defines (nothing executed, user prompted to clarify or told it was
      canceled).
- [ ] A full-stack Playwright test: a real question is typed into the running web app's chat, the
      widget appears, "Run" is selected via keyboard, and a result renders — exercising the real
      browser and a real backend turn, not just the Python harness function in isolation.
- [ ] No mechanism exists anywhere that allows a later `propose_temporary_datalog` call in the
      same session to skip confirmation.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: Off-topic acknowledgment before redirect
description:

`capability_manifest.py`) to explicitly permit a brief, honest acknowledgment of a general or
off-topic question (e.g. "what model am I talking to", "what color is the sky") before
redirecting the user back to P&ID review, instead of implying a bare non-answer or refusal. This
remains model-owned behavior driven by prompt text, not a new backend classifier — consistent
with the existing decision not to build a deterministic intent compiler.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `out_of_scope` policy text explicitly allows a short acknowledgment before the redirect.
- [ ] A small fixed set of real off-topic questions (e.g. "what model are you", "what color is
      the sky", "tell me a joke") run against a real tool-capable model produce a brief
      acknowledgment followed by a redirect back to P&ID review, checked as a regression prompt
      set rather than an exact-wording assertion.
- [ ] Existing `test_unrelated_question_is_redirected_without_backend_classifier` (or equivalent)
      continues to pass, confirming no backend classifier was introduced.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: Ad-hoc Datalog executes via real Souffle
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Replace the two-shape regex shim in the ad-hoc Datalog executor (which pattern-matches exactly
`answer("literal_id").` and `answer(x) :- reachable("some_id", x).` and silently returns zero
evidence for anything else) with a genuine `souffle` subprocess execution, the same way
`source_selection.py` already shells out to `souffle` today. The predicate set stays the current
narrow `{answer, reachable}` allowlist for this slice — expanding it is the next slice. The goal
here is fixing the silent-wrong-answer bug: a query outside the recognized shapes must now either
execute for real or fail with an explicit, specific validation/execution error, never silently
return "no matching objects" when the real issue is "this feature doesn't run your query."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirmed ad-hoc queries execute via a real `souffle` subprocess call, not text pattern
      matching.
- [ ] A query using only `answer`/`reachable` in the previously-supported shapes produces the same
      results as before (no regression for the two shapes already relied on).
- [ ] An invalid or unsafe query produces an explicit, specific error, never a silent empty
      result.
- [ ] A full-stack Playwright test: a real natural-language question that requires the confirmed
      query to actually execute (not just be accepted) is typed into the running web app, the
      widget from the confirmation-gate slice is used to Run it, and the browser shows a real,
      correct answer.
- [ ] A live-model check (real OpenRouter/BYOK tool-calling model, not a scripted provider): one
      real natural-language question is drafted into Datalog by the model, confirmed, executed,
      and produces a correct outcome.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34.2 (QA chat confirmation gate wiring, Claude-Code-style inline
  widget) — needs the pause/resume/confirm path working end-to-end for this to be demoable, not
  just unit-testable in isolation.
close_reason: Landed as abd4793. Real souffle subprocess execution (no regex shim), explicit errors on engine failure, legacy two shapes regression-covered, strengthened full-stack Playwright gate spec (passes; spec file remains uncommitted with the .2 frontend stack), live OpenRouter model check passes in ~9s (gpt-4o-mini drafts valid Datalog after the tool contract was added to the capability manifest).

title: Typed numeric-attribute predicate + threshold comparisons
description:
## Parent

## What to build

Add a typed numeric-attribute predicate to the EDB (derived from the existing symbol-typed
`node_attribute(id, attr_name, attr_value)` via Souffle's `to_number()` cast) so that rules and
ad-hoc queries can compare source-provided numeric values (e.g. a pressure rating already present
in the DEXPI source) against thresholds. This does not extend to calculations requiring external
formulas, correlations, or physical constants not present in the source graph — those remain out
of scope and must surface via the existing `source_data_unavailable` grounding posture, never be
invented or computed inline.

Demonstrate the new predicate through one concrete numeric-threshold check running through the
real Souffle rule-pack execution path landed in the "Rule packs run on real Souffle" slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A typed numeric-attribute predicate exists in the schema, correctly derived via
      `to_number()` from existing symbol-typed attribute facts, with no changes to fact export.
- [ ] At least one concrete rule using a numeric threshold comparison (e.g. a pressure-rating
      check) executes correctly via real Souffle and returns satisfied/violated/indeterminate as
      appropriate.
- [ ] A source object missing the relevant numeric attribute produces an explicit
      `source_data_unavailable`-equivalent outcome, not an invented value or false pass.
- [ ] A live-model check: a real natural-language numeric-threshold question run against a real
      tool-capable model produces a correct outcome using this predicate.

## Blocked by

  execution path to demonstrate the numeric predicate against.

title: Expand ad-hoc predicate contract to generic schema + rule-pack IDB
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Replace the ad-hoc query executor's hardcoded two-name predicate allowlist (`{answer,
reachable}`) with a predicate contract derived programmatically from the real schema: the generic
`graph_topology_semantics.dl` predicates, plus the IDB predicates declared by whichever rule
pack(s) are loaded in the current session, exposed read-only to ad-hoc queries. Rule packs are
not made mutable or extensible through this — only usable as join targets in the model's drafted
query. This unlocks recursion, joins, and real formal constraints in `propose_temporary_datalog`
that the two-shape shim could never support, and is the payoff for the real-execution work landed
in the previous slice.

The predicate contract must be derived from the schema/declarations, not hand-maintained as a
second list that can drift out of sync.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The model-facing predicate contract for `propose_temporary_datalog` reflects the current
      generic schema predicates plus the loaded rule pack(s)' IDB predicates, computed from the
      schema/rule-pack declarations rather than hardcoded.
- [ ] A confirmed query using a predicate beyond `{answer, reachable}` (e.g. a join against
      `direct_process_connection` or a loaded rule-pack predicate) executes correctly and returns
      real results.
- [ ] A confirmed query attempting to use a predicate not in the current contract (e.g. from an
      unloaded rule pack) is rejected with an explicit validation error.
- [ ] A live-model check: a real natural-language question requiring a real join or recursive
      constraint beyond the old shim's two shapes is correctly drafted and answered by a real
      tool-capable model.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34.4 (Ad-hoc Datalog executes via real Souffle) — expanding the
  predicate contract is only meaningful once queries actually execute for real.
close_reason: Landed as ad37cd35. Predicate contract is derived from graph facts/topology semantics declarations plus loaded rule-pack IDB declarations; confirmed ad-hoc programs execute over graph_facts + graph_topology_semantics + loaded rule-pack IDB + answer query. Covered generic schema join, unloaded-pack rejection, loaded-pack IDB execution, and live OpenRouter model drafting a direct_process_connection join.

title: Batched direction review, same widget pattern
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Extend `TurnLifecycleStore`'s review-required payload from a single review object to a list of
pending review items, so that a universal claim over multiple resolved objects (e.g. "do all
pumps have an isolation valve, a check valve, and a strainer") can surface more than one
ambiguous `direction review` (one per object with inferred rather than explicit flow direction)
in a single pause, instead of only supporting one pending item at a time.

Render all pending items in one instance of the boxed/numbered/keyboard-navigable widget built
for the ad-hoc confirmation gate — each item independently resolvable (confirm / reverse / mark
unknown) within that single widget, not N sequential pauses. Marking an item's direction unknown
leaves that specific object's outcome `indeterminate` for the claim permanently within that
evaluation (not re-askable).

The final answer for the universal claim must report satisfied/violated/indeterminate per object
individually, each with its own evidence chip and structural path witness — not a single flattened
yes/no.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The review-required event payload supports a list of pending direction-review items, not
      just one.
- [ ] A universal claim producing multiple ambiguous-direction objects in one evaluation pauses
      once, with all pending items visible in one widget.
- [ ] Each pending item can be resolved (confirm/reverse/unknown) independently of the others
      within that same widget, without forcing a single answer on all of them.
- [ ] An item marked unknown remains `indeterminate` for that claim and is not re-prompted within
      the same evaluation.
- [ ] The final answer reports per-object outcomes (satisfied/violated/indeterminate) with
      individual evidence chips, not a single flattened result.
- [ ] A full-stack Playwright test: a real universal question over multiple objects with at least
      two objects needing direction review is run against the real web app, and the batched
      widget with multiple independently-resolvable items is exercised end-to-end in the browser.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34.6 (Expand ad-hoc predicate contract to generic schema + rule-pack
  IDB) — needs a real multi-object universal-claim query capability to produce multiple ambiguous
  directions in one evaluation.
close_reason: Landed as 002ea67. Direction-review pause payload now carries direction_reviews[] while preserving legacy direction_review; API accepts batched per-item decisions; UI renders one batched widget with numbered independently-resolvable items; unknown decisions become indeterminate per-object outcomes. Validated with focused pytest/API checks, frontend node tests, and typecheck; Playwright remains blocked by unrelated upload/filechooser stack flakiness.

title: Enable model-planned retrieval and generated-logic escalation
description: Expose constrained read-only topology and bundled-rule tools plus a confirmation-required propose_datalog_query capability to a tool-eligible model. The model owns bounded retrieval planning, conversational ambiguity, domain relevance, and deciding when existing tools are insufficient. A Datalog proposal produces generated logic and an engineer-readable restatement, then pauses for backend validation and user confirmation; it never executes directly. Do not build an application intent classifier.
notes:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Resolved during grill-with-docs: application owns safe tools and evidence; model owns planning and conversation. Read-only tools run immediately. propose_datalog_query is confirmation-required and receives the predicate contract, allowed output shape, restrictions, prior context, and relevant IDs resolved through retrieval, not the full fact database by default.

title: Generate graph-grounded explanations from witnessed topology evidence

Backend evidence metadata remains authoritative for provenance, trust, direction, review status, and limitations; unknown evidence kinds degrade to generic presentation.

title: Align Datalog semantics with witnessed raw-graph topology
description: Generate Datalog facts and derived predicates from the pyDEXPI full graph using the same topology interpretation contract as direct graph operations. Ensure result bindings and rule outcomes resolve to complete structural path witnesses and canonical raw facts.
delete_reason: Superseded implementation breakdown; retain PRD epic only

title: Return justified tri-state rule evaluation outcomes
description: Represent every rule evaluation as satisfied, violated, or indeterminate with evidence. Satisfaction requires proof over the defined claim and scope. Absence-based violation requires complete evaluated scope and scope-completeness evidence. Apply claim-aware truncation: retain all grounded partial evidence, allow witnessed existential matches and counterexamples where logically sufficient, and return indeterminate when truncated coverage cannot prove a universal or absence conclusion.
notes:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Resolved during grill-with-docs: negative rule outcomes require both the fully evaluated bounded scope and evidence explaining why traversal was complete.
delete_reason: Superseded implementation breakdown; retain PRD epic only

title: Separate query confirmation from reusable rule-pack trust
description: Treat all model-generated Datalog plus restatement as temporary confirmed query pairs, even when generated text appears source-independent. Never infer, suggest, or persist generated logic as a reusable rule in OSS v1. Only exact versioned repository-bundled rule-pack rules are reusable and trusted. User-uploaded executable rule packs, generated-query promotion, and durable user rule storage are out of scope.
notes:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Resolved during grill-with-docs: OSS v1 supports repository-bundled executable rule packs only. User-uploaded executable packs, Markdown policy-source uploads, policy-to-rule synthesis, and generated-query promotion are disallowed. Those capabilities belong to a future paid rule-authoring tier.
delete_reason: Superseded implementation breakdown; retain PRD epic only

title: Store session-scoped direction review annotations
description: Attach user confirmation, reversal, or unknown direction to an exact structural path witness and evaluation boundary in the active review session. Reuse it for later questions only while that exact witness and boundary remain unchanged. New upload, changed path, or changed boundary invalidates it. Preserve original evidence status, never mutate the pyDEXPI full graph, and identify reused direction as user-confirmed.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Confirm, reverse, and unknown choices create session direction annotations.
- [ ] The annotation references the exact structural path witness and evaluation boundary.
- [ ] A later operation with the identical witness and boundary reuses the annotation.
- [ ] A new upload, changed path, or changed boundary does not reuse the annotation.
- [ ] Reused direction is reported as user-confirmed, never explicit DEXPI evidence.
- [ ] Reviewed annotations can unblock and rerun operations requiring direction.

title: PortLog Harvey-style review doctrine (wayfinder map)
description:
## Destination

Lock a PortLog product doctrine (in `docs/` + `CONTEXT.md` glossary updates) for a Harvey-style review workspace: answer posture, document analysis, and patch proposals — with pillar and trust boundaries sharp enough that a later PRD can pick the first engineering wedge without reopening product identity.

This map ends when the doctrine is written and agreed. It does **not** end with a PRD, a shipped feature, applied DEXPI write-back, or Harborfield commercial packaging.

## Notes

- **Domain:** process engineering; DEXPI / P&ID; multi-document review; grounded QA harness.
- **Skills each session consults:** grilling, domain-modeling; use ubiquitous-language when editing CONTEXT.md.
- **Identity (locked):** review workspace — not chat-with-a-drawing, not twin/simulation product.
- **Pillars (locked):** (1) answer posture (2) document analysis (3) patch proposals.
- **Modes (locked):** Inspect / Verify / Propose.
- **Trust strata (locked):** verified graph facts / provisional document claims / judgments.
- **Answer posture (locked via 3ebh.2):** modes×outcomes — Inspect/Verify/Propose/Redirect; Verify uses satisfied/violated/indeterminate; Inspect never issues Verify verdicts (`evidence_cited` / `evidence_insufficient`); auto-route Inspect/Redirect; Verify/Propose explicit-only; mandatory mode+fields disclosure; never invent support.
- **Evidence-on-drawing (locked as requirement):** when possible, show document/evidence hits on the P&ID/PFD; mechanism is fog.
- **Hard outs (locked):** applied DEXPI rewrite; silent auto-fix; twin/world-model simulation as a deliverable; OCR-first; automatic “trusted compliance” from model prose.
- **In (locked):** directed process-engineering chat; grounded Inspect over uploaded standards/PDFs + P&ID (not necessarily logic-proved).
- **vs rmso:** sibling maps. rmso proves cheap-model logic-grounded verdicts. This doctrine is broader: logic is the highest-trust path when available, not the only answer class.
- **Harborfield:** guiding principle for PortLog as OSS BYOK harness / precursor only — not commercial packaging in this effort.
- **Plan, don't do:** resolve decisions; write doctrine only via its ticket; do not ship product features from this map.

## Decisions so far

<!-- index — one line per closed ticket -->
- [Decide corpus object: DEXPI spine+attachments vs multi-artifact project](pydexpi-datalog-1-3ebh.1) — Near-horizon corpus = DEXPI spine for verified graph facts + chat-scoped attachments keyed across spines; doc-only pre-session allowed until a DEXPI is attached.
- [Lock answer-posture classes and disclosure rules](pydexpi-datalog-1-3ebh.2) — Modes×outcomes: Inspect/Verify/Propose/Redirect; Verify triad; Inspect never verdicts (cited/insufficient); Propose linked non-applied; auto Inspect/Redirect, explicit Verify/Propose; mandatory mode+fields disclosure; LLM call mechanics fog.
- [Decide what document analysis produces](pydexpi-datalog-1-3ebh.3) — Provisional typed claim ledger with revision-pinned evidence, reconciliation/link-resolution work, explicit governing-source decisions, and explicit-only non-executable formalization candidates.
- [Decide patch proposal kinds (non-applying)](pydexpi-datalog-1-3ebh.4) — Typed non-applied graph, reconciliation, and action/change-order proposals; reviewable multi-edit packages, provenance/baseline/impact, lifecycle, and mandatory limits.
- [Decide fate of hybrid advisory rule packs vs agent skills](pydexpi-datalog-1-3ebh.5) — Operator-managed versioned guidance skills guide Inspect/Propose, disclose themselves, and can recommend but never activate executable rules.
- [Decide Electron shell and Pi integration boundary](pydexpi-datalog-1-3ebh.7) — Electron shell; PortLog owns canonical review/chat state; Pi SDK is a replaceable adapter behind PortLog tools, with sidecar/OAuth fit-gap charted separately.
- [Write PortLog Harvey-style doctrine into docs/ and CONTEXT.md](pydexpi-datalog-1-3ebh.6) — Doctrine captured in `docs/portlog-harvey-review-doctrine.md`; glossary sharpened in `CONTEXT.md`.

## Not yet specified

- How many LLM calls / tool graphs implement each answer posture (deferred from 3ebh.2; UX disclosure locked).
- Exact first vertical-slice engineering wedge (explicitly deferred past this doctrine).
- How evidence-on-drawing is implemented (requirement locked; mechanism not).
- Twin / world-model later ladder (guiding only).
- OCR / scanned plants (hard out for this map).
- How existing backlog PRDs (37x / 2c5 / 2ki / hybrid packs) should be re-ranked after doctrine lands.
- Fused cross-diagram graph / joined multi-DEXPI traversal (wanted later; explicitly not locked by 3ebh.1).
- Multi-spine Verify producing one joined verdict (wanted later; not in near-horizon doctrine).
- Auto-promotion of document claims into verified graph facts (wanted later; claims stay provisional for now).
- Project-as-corpus — making `review project` the corpus object instead of chat + sessions (wanted later; project stays chat grouping).

## Out of scope

- Building or applying corrected DEXPI / silent autocorrection.
- Redesigning or absorbing **Grounded verdict engine for DEXPI/P&ID compliance** (rmso) — sibling proof spine.
- Harborfield enterprise packaging / monetization.
- Picking and implementing the concrete first engineering demo slice.
close_reason: Harvey-style review doctrine decisions are recorded, written into docs and glossary, and validated.

title: Decide corpus object: DEXPI spine+attachments vs multi-artifact project
description:
## Question

What is the primary corpus object for PortLog under the Harvey-style review doctrine?

Grill with concrete scenarios until one of these (or a precise hybrid) is locked:

1. **Single-DEXPI spine + attachments** — one drawing is the structural spine; other docs attach as evidence keyed to its entities/findings.
2. **Multi-artifact project** — a project/matter can hold multiple drawings + registers + narratives as first-class peers, with identity reconciliation across them.
3. A **named hybrid** with explicit rules for which artifact is structural spine when multiple DEXPI files exist.

Constraints already locked on the parent map:
- Review workspace identity; Inspect / Verify / Propose
- Trust strata: graph facts / document claims / judgments
- Directed PE chat + grounded standards Inspect in; applied write-back out
- Evidence-on-drawing is a pillar requirement (mechanism fog)

Answer must state: the chosen object, what “upload a review” means for the user, and what is deferred.
close_reason: Locked DEXPI spine + chat-scoped attachments; doc-only pre-session; deferred fused graph / multi-spine Verify / auto-claim promotion / project-as-corpus to fog

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Resolution

**Primary corpus object (near-horizon doctrine):** DEXPI spine + attachments.

### Locks
1. **Verified graph facts** live only in a `single-file review session` over one DEXPI spine (existing glossary boundary stands: fact bases never merge across sessions).
2. **Non-DEXPI documents** (datasheets, indexes, narratives, procedures, standards/PDFs) are **attachments**, not peer structural sources. They yield provisional document claims / evidence, not automatic graph facts.
3. **Attachments are chat-scoped** and may be keyed to entities across multiple attached DEXPI spines. They are not exclusively bound to a single “active” spine.
4. **Doc-only pre-session is allowed:** user may upload documents first and run Inspect (with abstain/indeterminate when evidence is insufficient). Attaching a DEXPI promotes the work into a full review session with a structural spine (Verify/Propose become meaningful against that spine).
5. **Multi-DEXPI in one chat** stays the existing model: fan-out per session, compose in prose — **no fused cross-diagram graph** in this doctrine horizon.
6. **`review project`** remains a chat-grouping workspace, **not** the corpus object.

### What “upload a review” means
- **Full path:** upload/attach at least one DEXPI → session spine + optional chat attachments.
- **Pre-path:** upload documents only → doc-only pre-session (Inspect); add DEXPI when ready for spine-backed Verify/Propose.

### Explicitly deferred (map fog — wanted later, not locked here)
- Fused cross-diagram graph / joined traversal
- Multi-spine Verify producing one joined verdict
- Auto-promotion of document claims to verified graph facts
- Project-as-corpus (project replacing chat+sessions as the corpus object)

Sibling: does not redesign rmso; does not implement 2c5 — aligns with existing single-file session + chat fan-out vocabulary.

title: Lock answer-posture classes and disclosure rules
description:
## Question

What concrete **answer-posture classes** does PortLog use, and what disclosure rules attach to each?

This is classification of *how* we respond — not an allow/deny gate. Locked intent from charting:

- Respond to every process-engineering-directed question.
- Prefer logic-grounded Verify when the expressible island can carry it.
- Otherwise cited Inspect / evidence when available.
- **Abstain or mark indeterminate when evidence is insufficient** — never invent support.
- Never dress non-Verify up as Verify.
- Logic is best-effort high-trust path; not every doc question gets a proof (sibling to rmso, not equal).

Grill until the doctrine can name the classes (e.g. Verify / Inspect / Indeterminate / Abstain / out-of-domain redirect — exact names TBD) and the user-visible disclosure for each.

Answer must include: class list, when each applies, and mandatory disclosure text/shape.
close_reason: Locked modes×outcomes; Inspect never verdicts; auto Inspect/Redirect; explicit Verify/Propose; mandatory disclosure; LLM call mechanics fog

comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text:
## Resolution

### Shape
Answer posture = **modes × evidence outcomes** (not a flat allow/deny list).
User-visible trust/disclosure only; **LLM API call graphs / tool routing mechanics = fog** (not locked here).

### Modes (every response declares one)
- **Inspect** — evidence lookup / compare across DEXPI spine + attachments (and disclosed general PE knowledge when appropriate). Never issues Verify verdicts.
- **Verify** — scoped deterministic rule/check over expressible island; outcomes only: `satisfied` | `violated` | `indeterminate` (existing glossary).
- **Propose** — reviewable non-applied patch suggestion; must link a finding or Inspect observation; must state not applied; must show evidence.
- **Redirect** — not PE/corpus work; **no plant judgment**. General EPA/standards Q&A with disclosed `answer source posture` stays **Inspect**, not Redirect.

### Inspect evidence states
- `evidence_cited` — usable citations/excerpts (optionally evidence-on-drawing later).
- `evidence_insufficient` — respond but **abstain from plant judgment** (no separate Abstain mode).

### Mode selection (locked)
- **Auto-route** Inspect and Redirect from question + corpus.
- **Verify and Propose only when explicitly invoked** (slash / chip / button / equivalent) — do not silent-promote into them.
- Disclosure always shows which mode ran (and override if any).

### Mandatory disclosure
Every answer shows **mode** plus class-specific fields:
- Verify: rule outcome + evidence/witnesses
- Inspect: `answer source posture` (graph / attachments / general / mix) + citations or `evidence_insufficient`
- Propose: linked finding/observation + non-applied + evidence
- Redirect: why redirected

### Explicitly not decided here
How many LLM calls / which tools implement each mode (implementation fog).

title: Decide what document analysis produces
description:
## Question

When PortLog analyzes non-DEXPI documents (datasheets, indexes, narratives, procedures, uploaded standards/PDFs), what **work products** does document analysis produce for the doctrine?

Candidates to grill:
- Provisional **document claims** keyed to graph entities (or orphans)
- **Reconciliation reports** (missing tags, type mismatches, numeric conflicts)
- **Evidence packs** for assets/findings (citations + excerpts)
- Something else — name it

Locked: claims are not automatically trusted graph facts; evidence-on-drawing is a requirement when possible; OCR-first is out.

Answer must state: primary artifacts, trust status of each, and what is explicitly not produced in this doctrine’s first horizon.
notes:
2026-07-28 grilling decision — primary durable work product: a provisional claim ledger. A claim records an extracted/asserted statement from an attached non-DEXPI document and its evidence. Claims link to a DEXPI graph entity when resolution is sound; otherwise they remain explicit orphans. Evidence packs (citations/excerpts) and reconciliation reports are derived views/artifacts over the ledger, not independent truth stores. Claims never automatically become verified graph facts.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — every claim shown to the user or used by reconciliation must carry explicit origin (document_extracted vs model_inference), explicit entity-link state (linked/orphan/ambiguous), and a non-empty evidence_refs[] collection. Each evidence reference is pinned to the source document revision and is a typed anchor: e.g. PDF page+bbox or section/span; spreadsheet sheet+cell/range; drawing/image/vector region. Excerpt or OCR text is optional per anchor, never fabricated, and not required where it is meaningless. A multi-source inference cites every supporting anchor. Content without typed evidence is not a ledger claim.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — when a provisional document claim conflicts with a verified graph fact, document analysis creates a reconciliation item, not an engineering finding. The item preserves both values, their evidence_refs, and the comparison basis. It is neither a Verify satisfied/violated verdict nor a patch proposal, cannot mutate a graph fact, and becomes a finding/proposal only through a later explicit user-directed workflow.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — automatic claim-to-graph links require a deterministic, unambiguous identity mapping (e.g. exact or normalized tag identity). Model/fuzzy matches never create a link by confidence threshold; they remain explicit ambiguous candidates or orphans until an engineer confirms the identity.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — evidence packs are on-demand projections over the claim ledger's revision-pinned evidence_refs plus deterministic review artifacts. They may be snapshotted only as part of an explicit export, but are never a separately mutable evidence authority.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — an ambiguous claim persists an ordered candidate set of possible graph entity IDs and each candidate's matching basis. The claim remains link_state=ambiguous until an engineer explicitly confirms one candidate; no reconciliation, finding, Verify evaluation, or proposal may treat a candidate as a graph link.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — source assertions and claims are immutable per source revision. Newer material does not automatically become governing truth. A governed review may rely on an explicit governing-source selection made by an authorized engineer or project policy, scoped to a review/as-of date and recorded with its basis. Same-document formal revision lineage or explicit supersession may be surfaced as evidence for that selection but does not silently select a value. Without a selection, competing assertions remain an unresolved source disagreement; Inspect shows the evidence, while any Verify premise requiring one value is indeterminate or unavailable. The selected assertion does not erase competing historical claims or mutate a verified graph fact.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — a governing-source selection applies to a named review scope and as-of date. It can select a document revision or a source class for that scope; entity/attribute-specific overrides are permitted only as separately explicit recorded decisions. There is no project-wide implicit switch and no retrospective rewrite of other review scopes.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — first-horizon authorization is an explicit, auditable operator decision. Record the local/signed-in operator identity, time, review scope, selected source, and rationale/basis. No enterprise approver-role model or automatic project policy can silently choose a governing source in this doctrine.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — reconciliation items have persistent lifecycle states open, acknowledged, and superseded. Acknowledged records operator review of the disagreement, not a claim that it was fixed or reconciled; superseded records that a subsequent selected source/revision replaced the item's comparison basis. Neither state mutates source assertions/graph facts or creates a Verify outcome.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — standards/procedures/narratives produce provisional requirement claims with typed evidence_refs. Ingestion does not create executable rules, EDB facts, or compliance outcomes. Only an explicit Propose/formalize request may generate a candidate logic expression against PortLog's known logic schema and predicate vocabulary (which may include approved EDB and derived/IDB predicates), linked to a requirement claim; the candidate is non-executable and non-promoted until the distinct human review/promotion path validates it.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — document analysis uses one generic claim envelope, not separate ledgers. All claims share revision-pinned evidence, origin, trust, entity-link, candidate-link, and reconciliation/authority rules. Typed kinds distinguish at least property, relationship, requirement, and document-control assertions; later kinds may extend the vocabulary without bypassing the common trust boundary.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — qualified source language is a valid claim, not a reason to discard the statement. Preserve modality and any stated condition/exception as claim content; e.g. “normally” becomes an evidenced expectation that it should happen, never an unconditional fact or universal requirement. When applicability remains ambiguous, disclose that ambiguity in the claim and Inspect presentation; do not silently strengthen or omit the qualifier.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — document analysis automatically runs reconciliation as a non-verdict background step after claims are available and a review scope/active source selection exists. It creates or refreshes open reconciliation items only; no background result becomes a finding, Verify outcome, proposal, or mutation.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — orphaned/ambiguous claims are surfaced in a persistent link-resolution queue with their typed evidence_refs and, for ambiguous claims, their candidate mappings/matching bases. They do not participate in reconciliation until an engineer resolves the graph link.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — an engineer-confirmed document-label-to-graph-entity mapping may be reused for other claims from that exact document revision, retaining confirmation provenance. It is not a project-wide alias: a later document revision must explicitly inherit or re-establish the mapping before reuse.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — if analysis cannot establish a usable revision-pinned typed evidence reference for a potential statement, persist a document-analysis diagnostic/coverage gap and no ledger claim. A local extraction failure does not invalidate other anchored claims from the same document; no unanchored or low-confidence pseudo-source may enter the ledger.
close_reason: Claim-ledger work products, evidence/provenance, reconciliation, governing-source, standards-formalization, and non-output boundaries decided.

title: Decide patch proposal kinds (non-applying)
description:
## Question

Which **patch proposal kinds** are in-doctrine for Propose mode, given patches are reviewable recommendations and **not** applied write-back?

Grill kinds such as:
- Graph/topology edit suggestions (e.g. missing discharge check valve on a segment)
- Document-claim corrections (datasheet vs drawing mismatches)
- Engineer instruction / change-order style prose
- Others — only if sharp

Hard out on the parent map: applied DEXPI rewrite; silent auto-fix.

Answer must list allowed kinds, required fields (finding link, evidence, atomicity), and what Propose explicitly refuses to claim.
notes:
2026-07-28 grilling decision — allowed first-horizon Propose kinds are one common non-applying proposal envelope with typed kinds: (1) graph/topology change recommendation, (2) document/reconciliation-resolution recommendation, and (3) engineering action/change-order recommendation. A proposal is not applied DEXPI write-back, document editing, graph mutation, rule-pack promotion, or an automatic governing-source selection.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — a proposal may contain multiple individually identified edits/recommendations when they form one engineering change package; do not force a one-target-only proposal shape.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — multi-edit proposals record child-level accept/reject/needs-revision decisions. Accepted child edits form an explicit accepted subset; rejected or needs-revision child edits are issued as a separately identified derived remainder proposal, preserving their evidence and review state. Do not leave a single ambiguous partially-accepted package.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — every proposal must link to both (a) a review trigger: a finding, reconciliation item, requirement claim, or explicit user request; and (b) typed revision-pinned evidence_refs. A free-floating model suggestion is not a PortLog proposal.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — every proposal records its active baseline: relevant graph/document/review-scope revisions, affected targets, expected benefit, and explicit assumptions/unknowns. It remains reviewable after those inputs change but must be marked stale/needs-rebase rather than imply clean applicability.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — proposal lifecycle is draft, proposed, accepted, rejected, needs-revision, or superseded. Accepted means the operator/engineer endorses the recommendation for downstream work/export only; it never applies a change inside PortLog. Superseded preserves a proposal's historical record after it is replaced or rebased.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — every Propose result explicitly discloses that it is a non-applied recommendation, identifies whether its rationale rests on graph evidence, provisional document claim, and/or judgment, and lists validation/approval still required. It must not imply design approval, field implementation, or compliance satisfaction.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — a proposal carries typed recommended operations plus engineer-readable explanation. A graph/topology proposal has typed suggested change operations; a document/reconciliation proposal has an explicit suggested source/authority resolution; an action/change-order proposal has structured requested action, owner/recipient, and verification request. Each retains rationale and typed evidence_refs; no typed operation is applied by PortLog.
close_reason: Allowed proposal kinds, multi-edit review semantics, required provenance/baseline/impact fields, lifecycle, disclosure limits, and typed representation decided.

title: Decide fate of hybrid advisory rule packs vs agent skills
description:
## Question

What happens to **hybrid advisory rule packs** under the Harvey-style doctrine?

Charting note from the human: likes the idea, but users realistically will not upload markdown requirement packs; packs may become agent `SKILLS.md`-like guidance; logic takes over when possible.

Grill until doctrine locks one stance, e.g.:
- Keep user-authored hybrid packs as optional power-user path
- Reposition packs as agent skill/context artifacts (not primary UX)
- Split advisory guidance vs executable rules differently
- Deprecate / narrow the existing hybrid-pack surface for PortLog OSS

Relate without absorbing: existing hybrid pack vertical slice / ADR 0013 work; do not redesign rmso.

Answer must state: user-facing role, authoring expectation, and relationship to Inspect / Verify / Propose.
notes:
2026-07-28 grilling decision — hybrid advisory packs are repositioned as curated PortLog/operator guidance skills and are not a normal user-facing Markdown upload workflow. Engineers attach ordinary engineering documents; curated skills shape agent behavior/context for Inspect and Propose. This does not eliminate separately reviewable executable rules or promoted rule packs.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — guidance skills are PortLog/operator-managed and versioned: bundled or installed by an OSS operator outside ordinary review workflow. There is no normal engineer-facing in-app skill authoring/upload surface in this doctrine horizon.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — skills may guide Inspect and Propose only: they can prioritize questions/retrieval, shape explanations, and inform candidate proposals. They never supply a Verify premise, rule evaluation, or outcome; Verify uses only explicit validated executable rules plus deterministic evidence.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — when a skill materially guides an Inspect answer or Propose recommendation, disclose the skill's name and version and clearly distinguish advisory guidance from document/graph evidence. Skill prose is never itself evidence for an engineering fact.

2026-07-28 grilling decision — a guidance skill may recommend a compatible validated rule pack or help draft an explicit formalization proposal, but may never attach, activate, or execute a rule pack itself. Verify begins only after explicit rule-pack selection/attachment and deterministic execution.
close_reason: Curated-skill user role, operator authorship, mode authority, disclosure, and explicit rule-pack boundary decided.

title: Write PortLog Harvey-style doctrine into docs/ and CONTEXT.md
description:

title: Decide Electron shell and Pi integration boundary
description:
Plan/decide only; no product implementation. Locked shell direction: Electron desktop harness. Preserve PortLog Python/Soufflé engine, typed review API, artifact store, catalog, and review state machine. Keep hosted-web fate explicitly deferred. Clarify OAuth separately from runtime: target local desktop provider authentication, but prove the Pi/OAuth integration path before promising it.

PortLog owns project/review/chat state, canonical user-visible message bodies/order/status, deterministic artifacts, evidence, findings, proposals, and approval decisions. Pi is a replaceable adapter. A Pi session is linked to one PortLog turn/run by immutable IDs, but Pi JSONL is never used to reconstruct or alter PortLog chat history.

First integration layer: full Pi coding-agent SDK behind PortLogAgent. Use custom PortLog capability tools and disable coding-oriented built-ins. Escalate to pi-agent-core/pi-ai only when a concrete public-seam failure requires it; fork only if lower-level Pi packages cannot meet a proven runtime invariant.

Do not declare pi-gui base/reference until the separately charted custom-driver/sidecar spike is assessed.
notes:
2026-07-28 decision — canonical transcript authority: PortLog owns message bodies, their ordering, turn status, cancellation/resume state, and user-visible chat history through its project/chat model and server-owned TurnLifecycleStore. This preserves existing replayable review turns and deterministic evidence linkage. Pi JSONL is non-canonical adapter telemetry: optional local diagnostic/recovery data for a Pi invocation, disposable and rebuildable from a PortLog turn plus selected context. A Pi session may be linked to exactly one PortLog turn/run by immutable IDs, but JSONL is never used to reconstruct or alter PortLog chat history. If Pi cannot operate under that constraint, use a lower-level Pi package or do not adopt Pi for the runtime. This supersedes the ambiguous phrase “Pi owns the conversational transcript.”

2026-07-28 decision — first Pi integration layer: use the full Pi coding-agent SDK behind the PortLogAgent adapter for the first Electron prototype. Use PortLog custom capability tools and disable coding-oriented built-ins. This is a provisional adoption seam, not a fork and not permission for Pi types, JSONL, or compaction semantics to escape into PortLog’s domain API. Escalate to pi-agent-core/pi-ai only when the custom-driver spike finds a concrete public-seam failure.

Canonical-source verification, 2026-07-28: GitHub resolves legacy badlogic/pi-mono to repository ID 1035029907, canonical identity earendil-works/pi (API reports fork=false). The intended upstream dependency is therefore @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent from earendil-works/pi, not pi-gui and not an unverified Pi fork. SDK surface checked at upstream main commit 063fb963c5c33d099faa593d17e60e0a875430cd: SessionManager.inMemory(), noTools/customTools, custom ModelRuntime authPath or CredentialStore, and lifecycle event subscription are documented. Pin a release/version during implementation; main-branch docs establish only the available seam, not a release guarantee.

Electron packaging, selected OAuth-provider interoperability, and sidecar supervision remain unproven and are charted as the child spike.
close_reason: Electron, canonical transcript ownership, and first Pi SDK adoption boundary decided; implementation proof is charted separately.

title: Spike Pi SDK adapter and Electron review sidecar
notes: 2026-07-28 final decision — PortLog will use its own minimal Electron shell. Pi is an optional, capability-bounded embedded agent/auth integration only; it does not own PortLog review/chat/artifact authority and pi-gui is reference-only. The shell supervises PortLog’s local Python+Soufflé sidecar and serves the existing review UI. Fresh OAuth /login remains intentionally unexercised because it would mutate an existing credential session; safe AuthStorage provider-status probing is sufficient for this throwaway decision spike.
close_reason: Electron shell selected; Pi integration boundary and packaging spike complete
