title: PRD: Establish the DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored fact substrate and derived Souffle semantics
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineering teams need a deterministic substrate for logical
programming over DEXPI 1.3 P&IDs before they can trust richer operator-facing
verification workflows.

The current repository already has useful scaffolding, a graph-mirrored export
seed, and an initial tracer-bullet verifier. What it does not yet have is a
fully explicit contract for turning the supported DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus into
graph-mirrored facts and then deriving reusable Souffle semantics from those
facts. Without that substrate, later rule work risks drifting into ad hoc
predicate design, fixture-specific shortcuts, or AI-generated rules without a
stable deterministic execution boundary.

## Solution

Build the next verifier substrate slice around DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored facts
and derived Souffle graph semantics.

The solution should treat `pyDEXPI` as the trusted extraction dependency for
DEXPI 1.3 XML-to-graph conversion, persist a verbose and generic canonical base
fact layer over the `pyDEXPI` full graph, and add a hand-authored generic graph
utility layer plus repo-owned edge-family classification policy in Souffle.

This slice should prove the substrate over the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture
corpus, document the contract sharply, and establish the behavioral test seams
that later pump-specific rules, rule packs, and AI-assisted rule synthesis can
rely on.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want DEXPI 1.3 to be the explicit authoritative input contract, so that the repository does not imply support for a different semantic ingestion model than the code actually uses.
2. As a maintainer, I want `pyDEXPI` to be treated as the trusted DEXPI 1.3 XML-to-graph extraction dependency, so that the project boundary between extraction and interpretation stays explicit.
3. As a rules author, I want the canonical base fact layer to mirror the `pyDEXPI` full graph, so that every downstream rule begins from a reproducible graph substrate.
4. As a rules author, I want the base export to remain intentionally verbose and generic, so that I do not lose evidence through premature schema curation.
5. As a maintainer, I want one persisted fact per extracted node, one per extracted edge, and one per attached attribute, so that the fact grain remains stable and auditable.
6. As a maintainer, I want previously unseen upstream attributes to survive export automatically, so that new DEXPI 1.3 fixture shapes do not break the substrate.
7. As a rules author, I want the base export to avoid convenience predicates such as `pump/1`, so that interpretation stays out of the persisted contract.
8. As a maintainer, I want the contract to be defined over the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus, so that the substrate proves itself against real fixture breadth rather than one narrow example.
9. As a reviewer, I want the checked-in golden fixtures to be clearly documented as a seed set rather than the full contract boundary, so that future work does not mistake current goldens for full coverage.
10. As a rules author, I want the first derived Souffle layer to be generic and reusable, so that later rule families can build on it without rewriting graph logic.
11. As a rules author, I want reusable edge-family predicates such as `composition_edge/3` and `reference_edge/3`, so that downstream rules do not repeatedly join raw edge attributes by hand.
12. As a rules author, I want a cautious `candidate_topology_edge/3` predicate, so that topology traversal can begin before the project commits to a stronger process-topology interpretation.
13. As a rules author, I want family-specific direct adjacency helpers, so that each rule can choose the correct traversal semantics explicitly.
14. As a rules author, I want a simple recursive `reachable/2` predicate over candidate topology edges, so that I can ask whether something is downstream without building full path provenance first.
15. As a maintainer, I want the first utility layer to stay small and explicit, so that it does not accumulate broad helper predicates before real rules require them.
16. As a maintainer, I want the edge-family classification policy to live in Souffle, so that interpretation can evolve without changing the persisted export format.
17. As a reviewer, I want the derived graph semantics contract to name the initial predicate surface explicitly, so that the next implementation slice cannot drift into vague “some utilities later” language.
18. As a process engineer, I want verification to be documented as downstream of graph export plus derived semantics, so that the architecture is understood as layered rather than verifier-first.
19. As a maintainer, I want the contract docs to state clearly that convenience predicates and domain predicates belong in derived Souffle layers, so that no one silently moves interpretation into the exporter.
20. As a maintainer, I want outdated `DEXPI 2.0 semantic IR` language removed from the active glossary and contract docs, so that the written architecture matches the implemented boundary.
21. As a rules author, I want the first validation seam to be stable graph export over the DEXPI 1.3 corpus, so that later logic failures can be isolated from extraction/export failures.
22. As a rules author, I want the second validation seam to be focused tests over representative fixtures such as `E03`, `E06`, and `C01`, so that recursive and classified predicates can be checked against real graph shapes.
23. As a maintainer, I want synthetic examples to remain available for later isolated rule verification, so that future rule generation can be tested behaviorally and not only on noisy corpus fixtures.
24. As a future operator, I want later trusted rules to execute deterministically over the fact layer instead of relying on ad hoc AI answers, so that verification remains reproducible and auditable.
25. As a future AI-assisted rules author, I want a stable graph-mirrored substrate and reusable graph utilities, so that generated rules have a deterministic target surface to compile against.
26. As a compliance engineer, I want rule packs to remain distinct from policy source documents, so that natural-language standards can later synthesize candidate rules without being confused for executable logic.
27. As a reviewer, I want AI-generated rules to be treated as candidates that require behavioral examples, so that trust comes from deterministic execution rather than raw Datalog readability.
28. As a maintainer, I want the next slice to defer policy-document-to-rule-pack synthesis, so that the foundational substrate work is not swallowed by a much larger AI problem.
29. As a maintainer, I want the repo PRD and Beads issue record to describe the same substrate plan, so that future contributors do not read contradictory planning artifacts.
30. As an engineer extending the verifier later, I want explicit derived graph semantics contracts in the docs, so that new rule families can reuse the same vocabulary and testing seams.

## Implementation Decisions

- The authoritative input contract for this slice is DEXPI 1.3 only.
- `pyDEXPI` is the trusted extraction dependency for XML-to-graph conversion; this repository owns graph-to-facts export and Souffle-derived interpretation above that export.
- The canonical persisted layer is a graph-mirrored base fact layer over the `pyDEXPI` full graph rather than a raw XML fact tree or an early domain-curated schema.
- The canonical base fact layer is intentionally verbose and generic. It should preserve extracted nodes, extracted edges, and attached attributes without introducing rule-specific predicates.
- Unknown or newly observed upstream attributes should survive export automatically through generic attribute facts rather than causing schema failures.
- The canonical base layer should persist only the `pyDEXPI` full graph for now. Explicit raw XML containment facts are deferred unless a concrete future rule proves they are needed.
- The intended regression surface for the substrate is the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus, not only the current `E03`, `E06`, and `C01` golden seed set.
- The first derived Souffle layer should be hand-authored rather than generated from observed graph schema.
- The repo-owned classification policy should live in Souffle rather than in exporter code, so classified semantics can evolve without re-exporting the canonical fact layer.
- The initial derived predicate surface should be explicit: `composition_edge/3`, `reference_edge/3`, `candidate_topology_edge/3`, `downstream_candidate/2`, `downstream_composition/2`, `downstream_reference/2`, and `reachable/2`.
- `candidate_topology_edge/3` should be intentionally conservative rather than claiming that topology traversal is already fully trusted in every case.
- Direct adjacency helpers should stay family-specific. Broader union predicates such as `downstream/2` should be introduced only when a real rule or operator-facing query needs them.
- The first recursive utility should be `reachable/2` over `candidate_topology_edge/3`; ordered path reconstruction and full path provenance are deferred.
- Pump discharge YAML rules should sit above the generic base fact layer and derived graph semantics layer rather than embedding graph semantics themselves.
- Verification commands should be documented and treated as consumers of the export-plus-derived-semantics substrate, not as the primary architectural center.
- The rule trust model for later AI-assisted work should be behavioral: candidate rules become trustworthy only after deterministic execution against positive and negative examples.
- Single rules and rule packs remain distinct units. Individual rules are the unit of behavioral debugging; rule packs are the unit of versioned promotion and deployment.
- Policy source documents, rule packs, and rule-pack synthesis are distinct concepts and should remain separate in the glossary and contract docs.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests should assert external behavior and stable contracts, not implementation details or private helper structure.
- The highest seam for this slice is the `export-facts` behavior over the parseable DEXPI 1.3 fixture corpus. Tests at this seam should verify deterministic persisted graph-mirrored facts, provenance, and automatic preservation of observed attributes.
- A second high seam should cover the derived graph semantics layer on representative fixtures such as `E03`, `E06`, and `C01`, validating classified edge families, family-specific downstream helpers, and recursive `reachable/2`.
- Later synthetic examples should be used for isolated rule-shape verification, but the current substrate slice should prefer real DEXPI 1.3 fixtures wherever possible.
- Tests should confirm that the base export does not emit convenience predicates or domain predicates in the persisted artifact contract.
- Tests should verify that the current checked-in golden fixtures remain a seed set and that broader corpus coverage can be expanded without redefining the base contract.
- Tests should confirm that the derived classification policy lives above the persisted export and can change without changing the base fact artifact shape.
- Documentation-facing tests or fixture assertions should continue to use the repo’s existing black-box style around CLI commands and persisted artifacts rather than internal function mocks.
- Prior art already exists in the repository for export-facts CLI tests, checked-in golden graph facts, compile-rule CLI tests, and verifier-suite artifact tests. The new tests should extend those existing seams instead of inventing lower-level unit seams.
- Future AI-assisted rule verification should rely on positive and negative examples evaluated by the deterministic engine, not human review of raw Datalog syntax.

## Out of Scope

- DEXPI 2.0 as an active ingestion contract.
- A raw XML fact layer or XML-tree-first substrate.
- Automatic generation of domain predicates from unseen graph shapes.
- Full path reconstruction or ordered path evidence in the first derived utility slice.
- Pump-specific or rule-specific domain predicates in the persisted base export.
- DEXPI 1.2 as part of the current canonical substrate contract.
- Policy-document-to-rule-pack synthesis.
- Operator-facing dropdown UX for rule or rule-pack selection.
- Trusting AI to answer operator verification questions directly without deterministic execution.
- Human approval workflows for AI-generated rules beyond the defined behavioral-verification model.

## Further Notes

- The most important architectural protection in this slice is the boundary between generic persisted facts and derived Souffle interpretation.
- The base fact layer should be allowed to be verbose if that preserves reproducibility and future extensibility.
- The current checked-in documentation cleanup is part of the work because stale contract language would otherwise undermine the implementation slice.
- This PRD intentionally narrows the next step to substrate work. Richer operator rules, compliance rule packs, and AI-assisted synthesis remain downstream consumers of this layer rather than part of it.
close_reason: Completed DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored fact substrate, corpus coverage, derived graph semantics, verifier integration, behavioral harness, and documentation reframing; validation passed with ./.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests.

title: Harden the generic fact contract for unseen graph attributes
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-n2o "PRD: Establish the DEXPI 1.3 graph-mirrored fact substrate and derived Souffle semantics"

title: Synthetic benchmark truth-by-construction disagrees with real Souffle on check-valve
description:
## What's broken

tests/benchmark/test_synthetic_slice.py::test_constructed_truth_matches_real_souffle_rule_output fails:

    AssertionError: syn-small-01-check-valve: constructed truth disagrees with engine
    assert [] == ['syn-small-01-t0-pump']

The generator injects a check-valve violation and records syn-small-01-t0-pump as ground truth by construction. Running the real rule pack over that drawing's canonical base fact layer, walk_boundary yields no terminal_object row at all, so the engine reports zero violators.

## Why it matters

This slice's entire value is that ground truth follows from construction rather than hand labeling (3q1.11). When construction and the engine disagree, one of them is wrong and the benchmark cannot referee the arms it exists to compare. A reasoning-architecture benchmark (3q1) that scores arms against unverified truth reports a number nobody should trust.

Only the small check-valve case is asserted here; whether the same disagreement affects larger buckets or the diameter rule is unmeasured.

## Reproduction

Pre-existing and unrelated to the ArtifactStore work. Verified byte-identical failure on ad4a97e (before fcf8d70) and at HEAD:

    PYTHONPATH=. PYDEXPI_QA_PROVIDER=scripted .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmark/test_synthetic_slice.py::test_constructed_truth_matches_real_souffle_rule_output

Runs in about 1.5s standalone. The rest of tests/benchmark passes (301 of 302).

## Where to look

- pydexpi_datalog/benchmark synthetic generator: what the injected check-valve violation actually builds
- verification/souffle_rule_pack.py load_rule_datalog and the walk_boundary IDB: whether a terminal_object boundary is reachable for that construction
- Possibly related: pydexpi-datalog-1-22q2 (get_reachable_equipment reports isolation for nozzle-connected equipment) is also a traversal-semantics disagreement; a shared root cause in how nozzle-mediated connectivity is walked would explain both

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Determine which side is wrong: the generator's constructed truth or the rule/IDB
- [ ] Fix that side; do not adjust the assertion to match observed output
- [ ] State whether larger size buckets and the diameter rule share the defect
- [ ] tests/benchmark passes in full

title: Grounded verdict engine for DEXPI/P&ID compliance (wayfinder map)
description:
## Destination

A grounded **verdict engine** for process-engineering documents (DEXPI / P&ID): given a
compliance/retrieval question over a drawing, a minimal loop authors an **executable logic
program** grounded in the canonical EDB, executes it, and returns an **auditable verdict +
exhaustive witness set** -- proven on a **cheap model (DeepSeek v4 Flash)**, optimizing
**cost per correct, grounded answer**. High-assurance verdict product (fork I). NOT a
navigation/search product.

## Notes

- **rmso is the EVALUATION & PROOF spine, not a competing engine.** Re-audit (2026-07-16)
  found the engine itself is already designed in the backlog. rmso validates whether the
  engine-mediated grounded-verdict approach is worth building on a cheap model, at what
  cost, and feeds REQUIREMENTS back. It does not re-design the engine.
- **Engine design is OWNED by existing beads** (do not duplicate): 3qo (LLM-assisted logic
  requests: routing, predicate contract, bounded repair), 37x.22.34 (real Souffle execution
  for rule packs + ad-hoc Datalog; ADR 0008), 311 (async deontic compilation to Datalog).
- **Builds on / EXTENDS 3q1** (benchmark harness, hand-authored slice 3q1.10, Arm C
  real-Souffle sandbox, Harbor/KIRA spike) -- KEEP, do not delete. Only 3q1's "direct vs
  engine" question is answered.
- Domain: process engineering; DEXPI XML; P&ID; HAZOP/deontic compliance.
- Skills each session consults: grilling, domain-modeling, behavior-tdd, research.
- Research assets: docs/research/program-as-reasoning-prior-art.md;
  docs/research/is-the-engine-worth-it-2026-landscape.md. Papers: VeriCoT, LOGicalThought,
  ReTraceQA, Logic-LM, PAL.
- Locked premises: engine justified over BYOK-wrapper (grounding gap structural in 2026);
  reasoning = one executed grounded program; cheap-model-viable (DeepSeek v4 Flash);
  minimal harness; Souffle-core, multi-solver as fog; metric = cost per correct, grounded
  answer.

## Decisions so far

<!-- index; one line per closed ticket -->
- **rmso.4 CLOSED** — Pre-registered 9-entry general-agent vs logic-agent evaluation: exact verdict+witness qualification, safe replayable audit traces, mechanical program faithfulness, quality-before-cost ($/grounded credit), 5-minute episodes, and a hard $10 spend cap. Protocol: `docs/research/rmso.4-pre-registered-eval-protocol.md`.

## Not yet specified

- Per-step VeriCoT-style verification (fast-follow once faithful cheap-model authoring proven).
- Datalog -> ASP expansion if rules prove defeasible (reconciled via rmso.3 + 311).
- Product surface: verdict + audit-trail UI; regulatory packaging (EU AI Act high-risk).
- Loop philosophy fork: Python-orchestrated (3qo/37x.22.34 stance) vs autonomous-agent
  (Arm C stance) -- rmso's spike should measure which delivers grounded answers cheaply.
- Non-DEXPI (scanned) extraction -- consume/license, do not build.

## Out of scope

- **Designing the engine** (router / repair loop / real-Souffle execution / predicate
  contract) -- OWNED by 3qo, 37x.22.34, 311. rmso feeds requirements; it does not build a
  parallel engine.
- Building OCR/extraction models -- commoditized; we have DEXPI XML.
- Navigation/search-only product (fork II).
- Re-litigating "is symbolic reasoning worth it" -- answered.
- Deleting 3q1 / 3qo / 311 -- rejected; they are foundational or engine-owning.

title: Faithfulness spike: can DeepSeek v4 Flash author faithful Datalog over the EDB?
description:
## Question

Two hypotheses, measured **separately** (the spike currently conflates them):
- **H1 authoring feasibility**: can DeepSeek v4 Flash author a FAITHFUL Datalog/Souffle
  program (one that actually *means the question*) over the canonical EDB?
- **H2 value**: does the engine loop BEAT LLM-direct on grounding (exhaustive witnesses)
  on questions where grounding matters?
Gating feasibility test for the whole build.

## Not a rigged demo (read first)

A 5-question loop will NOT look cheaper/faster than one-shotting an LLM on easy questions.
Valid only on grounding-hard questions, run as a fair head-to-head that is allowed to KILL
the engine. Cost/latency alone is the wrong axis: for a verdict product the metric is cost
per *correct, GROUNDED* answer, and an ungrounded cheap answer is unshippable.
**A test that cannot produce a losing result for the engine is not a test.**

## Scope: obligations only (deontic guardrail)

Engine v1 answers OBLIGATION/PROHIBITION violation checks over ground facts
("every X must have Y" -> find X without Y). **Permission** ("may / is X allowed?") and
**defeasible-exception** ("prohibited unless exempted") questions are OUT of the engine's
verdict path for now (machinery deferred; gated by rmso.3). The spike MUST include >=1
permission/defeasible question and verify the engine **ABSTAINS** ("not soundly decidable
by the engine") instead of emitting an unsound verdict. Sound abstention PASSES; an
unsound "permitted"/"no_violation" FAILS.

## Question selection (mandatory)

- Draw from the hand-authored slice (known ground truth) PLUS the harder controlled set
  (sibling authoring ticket).
- Core = grounding-hard, MULTI-witness obligation checks (exhaustive enumeration) — the
  engine's signature claim. Exclude trivial single-fact lookups from the core.
- **Drawing-size control**: run each core question on BOTH a small drawing (LLM can read
  everything) and a large one (lost-in-the-middle bites), to separate reasoning wins from
  long-context artifacts.
- **Adversarial items (so the test can fail for the engine)**: >=1 shallow single-object
  question a cheap LLM nails; >=1 the engine should find hard; >=1 permission/defeasible
  item (expect engine ABSTAIN).

## Two arms, same questions

- A) LLM-direct baseline: cheap model, one-shot over the drawing, no engine.
- B) Engine loop (behavior pinned below).

## Arm B behavior (pinned)

1. Input = question + allowed grounded predicates (EDB/rule-pack schema) — NOT raw XML.
2. Author a program (query + any rules).
3. Execute for real against the EDB (souffle).
4. Observe compile/exec errors, empty/mis-shaped output, contract violations.
5. Revise from diagnostics; re-run; cap at N revisions.
6. Answer = executed output (verdict + witness tuples). Never answer from unexecuted
   reasoning.

## Measurements (per question, per arm, per drawing size)

- Verdict match; abstention correctness (permission item).
- Witness precision / recall / F1 vs ground truth (NOT exact-set-only).
- Faithfulness of arm B's final program: back-translate to NL, compare to the question.
- Cost, tokens, wall time, # revise rounds (arm B).
- **Blind/mechanical grading**: F1 computed by code vs ground truth; NO human
  "close enough" judgement. Bar pre-registered below.

## Pre-registered decision rule

- **GO** iff: H1 holds (faithful authoring) AND H2 holds (arm B mean witness-F1 clears a
  bar arm A cannot on grounding-hard items, at tolerable revise count) AND the engine
  correctly ABSTAINS on the permission/defeasible item.
- **NO-GO / rethink** if any of: arm A matches arm B witness-F1 (engine adds nothing);
  the win exists only on LARGE drawings (long-context artifact, not reasoning — reframe
  the claim honestly); Flash cannot author faithful programs; the engine emits an unsound
  verdict on the permission item; arm B needs an unreasonable revise count.
- Cost recorded as data, not the gate (n small); real cost-per-correct-grounded-answer
  metric decided in rmso.4 + a larger run.

## Budget

~$5-10 live calls (two drawing sizes doubles calls).
close_reason: Completed the frozen two-arm paid matrix; both arms failed 9/9 qualification, yielding pre-registered NO-GO / rethink.

title: Design the query router: logic-path vs neural-path + cheap-first cascade
description:
## Question

Produce ROUTER REQUIREMENTS for the engine beads (3qo / 37x.22.34); do NOT design a second router. 3qo already specifies routing (topology-logic / metadata / docs / missing-capability / clarification) and the predicate contract. rmso owns only the eval-driven requirements the router must satisfy: (1) deontic ABSTENTION (permission/defeasible -> abstain/HITL, never an unsound verdict); (2) cheap-first cascade, escalate-on-failure; (3) the routing distinctions the cost-per-correct-grounded-answer metric depends on. Feed these into 3qo/37x.22.34.
notes:
Eval evidence: formal frozen v3 run /tmp/rmso-scored-v3-j8sf was COMPLETE with Arm T 9/9 at $0.03149864 and Arm C 8/9 at $0.09163029. Arm T used seven reviewed-template routes plus two mechanical policy abstentions, zero fallbacks, and 69.4% lower cost per grounded credit. These nine questions are development/regression data; fresh holdout remains mandatory.

Eval-driven hybrid router requirements (fold into the existing 3qo / 37x.22.34 router; do not create a second router):
R1. Existing route decision artifact must distinguish deterministic_lookup, metadata, documentation, reviewed_template, generated_datalog, clarification, missing_capability, and policy_abstention. Neural text is never the verdict source.
R2. Cheap-first cascade: trusted deterministic lookup/rule-pack path when sufficient -> reviewed template binding -> Arm C generated Datalog -> missing-capability/abstention. Escalate only on an explicit failure; never silently change paths.
R3. Deontic gate runs before topology routing: permission or defeasible-exception requests return policy_abstention/HITL and must never reach monotone template or generated-Datalog verdict execution.
R4. A reviewed-template route is accepted only when category, parameter types, ontology labels, explicit closed-list completeness, graph scope, and direction preserve the request. Listed classes may be absent from the current drawing; reusable semantic scope must survive replay.
R5. Template validation failure, no-fit, execution failure, or faithfulness failure emits a typed fallback reason and escalates to generated Datalog within a bounded budget. A tidy but meaning-wrong result is a failure.
R6. Generated Datalog retains the existing predicate contract, engineer-readable restatement and confirmation gate, two bounded repairs, deterministic execution, and a faithfulness check after the initial draft and every revision. Exhaustion yields missing capability/HITL, not an LLM answer.
R7. Persist one auditable path trace: attempted paths in order, final route, template id/bindings or generated-program hash, validation/faithfulness outcome, fallback reason, provider attribution, deterministic result identity, and abstention reason. Preserve minimal artifacts rather than full prompts.
R8. Metrics required for release evaluation: end-to-end grounded credit and cost per credit; template coverage excluding policy abstentions; conditional template correctness; false-route rate; generated-authoring avoided; fallback rate/reasons; latency; provider cost by attempted and final path.
R9. Reviewed templates expose the SME-facing rule description plus bindings, not raw Datalog. Generated Datalog remains untrusted until the existing confirmation workflow.
R10. Release claim requires a fresh SME-certified unseen slice containing template-fit, no-fit, ambiguous, explicit/implicit class scope, directed/undirected, piping/I&C, and deontic cases. Correct conservative fallback counts as success; repeated patching against the frozen nine does not.
close_reason: Defined eval-driven template-first hybrid requirements R1-R10 from the formal Arm T 9/9 result; handed them to existing router/execution owners 3qo and 37x.22.34 plus the shared faithfulness gate rmso.6 without creating a duplicate router.

title: Silent fixture fallback masks a dead backend
description:
prepareReviewSession calls the Python backend and, when that call is not ok for any reason, returns a fabricated result built by parsing the XML in the browser layer: status ready, a graph of invented nodes, sourceScopeIds defaulting to pump-101. No Souffle runs, no artifacts are written, no evidence exists. The caller cannot tell.

For a tool whose entire claim is deterministic answers that show their work, this is the worst available failure mode. A backend that is down, misconfigured, rate-limited or rejecting auth produces confident fiction rather than an error, and the person reading it has no signal at all.

Found because the JWKS misconfiguration in bead 2k4k made the backend answer 401 to its own front end. That cause is fixed, but the mask is what made it survive several rounds of testing: three separate times a review appeared to succeed while doing nothing. On a slow free-tier instance, backend timeouts will be routine, so this gets more likely rather than less.

The fallback may have been a deliberate offline affordance once. If so it needs to be explicit and visibly labelled as unverified, not silently substituted for a real review.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] A backend failure surfaces as an error, not a ready result
- [ ] No response can claim ready without backend evidence behind it
- [ ] If an offline preview is wanted, it is labelled unverified in the UI
- [ ] A test asserts a failing backend does not yield status ready
- [ ] The same rule covers the other proxy helpers with fallbacks
close_reason:
prepareReviewSession no longer fabricates. A backend that does not answer now yields status failed with an empty graph, and the route returns 502 so the browser raises instead of rendering. Proven both ways against the running container: healthy backend returns 200 and the real parse, unreachable backend returns 502, status failed, zero nodes.

Worse than first described. The fallback did not parse the uploaded file at all -- graphFromXml cloned samplePidGraph, the bundled demo plant, and highlighted nodes whose tags happened to appear in the XML. A reviewer would have been shown someone else's P&ID with readable tags. Removed, along with a second instance of the same class in readTopology, which substituted the sample graph whenever a backend response carried no nodes.

Tests cover 401, 404, 500, 503 and a thrown fetch, asserting neither ready nor invented nodes. 138 frontend tests, 660 python, typecheck, ruff and oxlint clean.
